Recursive Industrial Intelligence

r4.0 · July 2026

Leonardo Stern · Independent researcher

A self-sustaining, self-expanding space industrial system is coherent as an argument; whether it is feasible or economical is a question for models. This paper combines the executed models with an explicit autonomous seed, its knowledge package, its material flows, and the dynamics by which it attempts to expand operating capacity.

Abstract

This paper develops and tests a conditional thesis: advanced AI, reusable launch, robotics, energy systems, and automated manufacturing could be combined into an industrial system beyond Earth that maintains and expands its own productive capacity. This paper expands the object of analysis from an abstract industrial substrate to a capacity-expanding autonomous seed: physical equipment, embodied autonomy, software and simulation, industrial memory, experimental capacity, and material-category-resolved supply. Part I implements a ten-sector, multisector capacity model with decomposed depreciation, repair, recycling, stockpiles, imports, common-cause shocks, and architecture-specific constraints for LEO, the lunar surface, and Mars. Its unit-invariant replication metric is balanced capacity doubling; its endpoint is realized post-shock growth, and its bottleneck diagnostic is a finite 1% supply-response test with explicit co-binding. The assumption ensembles produce outcomes ranging from collapse to sustained expansion, with electronics dominant on the Moon, electronics and power on Mars, and captured/recovered feed dominant in LEO. The ten-sector model begins with positive capacity in all ten sectors and omits construction lags, commissioning, yield ramps, and minimum efficient scales; its doubling times are stylized capacity-model first passages, not factory-construction or seed-commissioning forecasts. Part II builds an affine levelized-cost model for terrestrial and space compute, separating integrated disposable satellites from serviceable/reusable platforms. After completing the system boundary with communications, ground network, spacecraft bus, program NRE, insurance, regulatory and disposal costs, residual value, thermal margins, and separate financing, generic LEO compute costs 5.29 times Earth on the serviceable-platform architecture and 6.74 times Earth if integrated and disposable; the SpaceXAI AI1 disclosed-design case remains 3.17 and 3.80 times Earth, respectively. The analysis therefore supports neither a point forecast of autonomous industry nor present orbital-compute parity. It identifies the architecture-dependent measurements and demonstrations that would most change those conclusions. An 18-sector, 17-material-group integrated-bootstrap model then represents an installed operating seed — physical equipment with stylized autonomy, intervention, construction, and commissioning constraints — and asks how much installed mass is sufficient, whether its material graph can close first on the Moon and later across asteroidal sources, and whether aggregate operating capacity can double without routine human intervention. Under the declared central assumptions, the minimum-mass lunar design retaining an Earth-supplied strategic-material import stock is 217.0 t installed — 58.2 t (27%) of it that stock — but its slowest normalized sector falls to 0.54 operating cell-equivalents by year 40; the configured strict lunar-only source graph is structurally infeasible, with the shortfall quantified per material category; and a synthetic composite Moon–asteroid portfolio satisfies the same seed-LP constraints at 187.9 t, crosses two at 35.25 years, and reaches 3.28 sector-balanced equivalents at year 40. Keeping all 18 sectors stateful changes the interpretation: the intelligence–industry coupling is nearly inert in the material-starved terrestrial and lunar-bridge cases but operative in the Moon–asteroid network, where removing it reduces year-40 balanced capacity from 3.28 to 2.71. The assumed AI level also binds statically through seed feasibility. These are deterministic consequences of a stipulated architecture and assumption ensemble (Part I.8), not seed designs, engineering estimates, or forecasts. The model operationalizes the coupled loop and sharpens its material and autonomy conditions; it does not demonstrate that the assumed processes, source portfolio, AI gains, or industrial closure exist.

Keywords: recursive industrial improvement; space manufacturing; industrial closure; orbital compute; lunar industry; multisector capacity; autonomous industrial seed; embodied autonomy; lunar materials; techno-economics; Monte Carlo.

Executive Summary

This document examines one possible long-horizon infrastructure value of advanced AI, reusable launch, energy systems, robotics, and automated manufacturing: combining them into a recursively improving industrial system beyond Earth. This is not a comparative claim that the pathway outweighs health, science, terrestrial abundance, climate, governance, or other uses of advanced AI. The end state is not merely a rocket fleet, a settlement, a humanoid robot, or a frontier model, but a distributed industrial ecology able to sustain itself, expand productive capacity, and progressively reduce Earth dependence.

Three questions remain separate throughout: which uses of advanced AI most benefit humanity; which architecture creates the largest long-horizon physical-growth option; and which hypothesis best explains the observed corporate portfolio. The paper models the second and tests evidence relevant to the third. It does not rank the first against health, poverty reduction, science, climate, governance, or other welfare objectives.

Powerful AI could be transformative without any space-industrial program. Conversely, an industrial system that achieves embodied-production and reproductive-capital closure can compound under a bounded controller without open-ended AI self-improvement. Their conjunction may accelerate the pathway; neither thesis establishes the other.

Central proposition. Once a space-based industrial system can obtain local energy and materials, maintain its machinery, manufacture additional productive equipment, and coordinate itself through AI, the primary constraint shifts from acquiring terrestrial inputs to allocating productive throughput over time.

That proposition distinguishes two growth regimes. An orbital data center whose servers, structures, power systems, and replacements continue to be made on Earth is deployed capacity, not a self-expanding industry:

The role of off-Earth industry is to combine that endogenous growth regime with access to matter, energy, and usable area outside Earth’s biosphere and society-priced siting constraints. Earth-fed orbital compute can therefore raise intelligence at a constant deployment rate without crossing the industrial-reproduction threshold; the two cases must not be conflated.

The framework separates three closures. Verified AI-R&D closure can produce and safely deploy accepted successor improvements. Embodied-production closure can execute every task on the active industrial minimum cut with available sensors, actuators, experiments, and recovery. Reproductive-capital closure can replace and expand every indispensable capital stock after depreciation and obsolescence. None implies the others. When all are present, the digital and physical loops can reinforce one another:

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

Here ItI_t is the intelligence-capability index, 𝒄t\mathbf c_t is the vector of task coverage and autonomy, 𝑲t\mathbf K_t is installed productive capacity by sector, and CtC_t is usable compute. 𝑹t\mathbf R_t, EtE_t, HtH_t, DtD_t, and VtV_t are the limiting material-resource, energy, compute-hardware, data, and verification states. The τ\tau terms are stage-specific delays; 𝜹K\boldsymbol\delta_K and δC\delta_C are depreciation rates; the Γ\Gamma terms collect construction, commissioning, verification, and authorization gates; and Π\Pi imposes declared capability ceilings. The response functions are saturating, resource-bounded mappings, not constant gains. In plain language: better intelligence can improve automation; verified automation can expand productive capacity; commissioned capacity can add usable compute; and usable compute can support further verified intelligence improvement.

A dimensionless local diagnostic may be formed from the product of the four elasticities around this path, Gloc=ϵcIϵKcϵCKϵICG_{\mathrm{loc}}=\epsilon_{cI}\epsilon_{Kc}\epsilon_{CK}\epsilon_{IC}, or, for the complete coupled state, from the spectral radius ρ(Jt)\rho(J_t) of its one-step Jacobian. A value above one means only that a small perturbation is locally amplified at that state and under those active gates. It is not sufficient for physical closure, stable or safe operation, global growth, or indefinite improvement.

That coupled case is the strongest acceleration branch, not the definition of all endogenous growth. The central Moon–asteroid model still reaches balanced physical doubling in 36.75 years when digital capability growth is frozen, versus 35.25 years with both loops active; with capital reproduction blocked, digital improvement alone never produces physical doubling. Control and verification are separate constraints in every branch.

The economic argument compresses to two walls and two escapes. The capital wall: expansion purchased through markets runs into scarcity pricing and supply-elasticity limits as ambitions scale; the escape is self-replication, which re-denominates expansion from dollars into materials, energy, and time. The operating wall: on Earth, society-priced costs — land, permits, politics, waste heat — rise with scale and cannot be closed away; the escape is space, where permission attaches to the gateway rather than the complex. Both escapes pass through one passage: the bridge, in which the first self-replicating seed is bought at full market price, operated where depreciation is most severe, and financed by intermediate products.

This paper prices the passage and models the seed. Five headline results:

  1. The active bottleneck is architecture-specific. A unit-invariant finite-response diagnostic relaxes each material balance by 1%, then divides credit among rows whose positive response is within 5% of the largest. Electronics receives about 94–97% of co-binding credit on the lunar surface; electronics and power divide most credit on Mars; and capture/mining receives about 86–100% in LEO. The LEO architecture has no ore body and depends on captured and recovered feed. Import-cut experiments are small, margin-conditional samples, so their defensible executive-level result is ordinal rather than a precise frequency: import dependency is architecture-dependent, and electronics is often load-bearing where the sampled strategic-material gap is deepest. That identity is conditional on a homogeneous electronics-productivity assumption, not a measurement of real electronics closure.
  2. Balanced-capacity doubling and sustained expansion are different outcomes. The headline replication metric is λ(t) = min_j K_j(t)/K_j(0) ≥ 2: every modeled sector has doubled in its own capacity units. It is not a claim that a commissioned second physical factory exists. The endpoint records realized, post-shock growth; the pre-shock allocation endpoint remains a diagnostic. In the declared central sampling measure, expansion at year 30 occupies a much larger region than sustained positive realized growth throughout years 25–30. Median balanced doubling among sampled runs that reach it is about 26.0 years in LEO, 5.0 on the Moon, and 11.0 on Mars. Exact occupancy counts and intervals are reported in Part I.8. The Earth-import-cut LEO result is expressly conditional on continued capture feed and is not an autonomous-ecology result.
  3. The space-compute crossover is an architecture story, not a launch-price story. At central inputs, generic LEO compute is 5.29× Earth on a serviceable/reusable platform and 6.74× if the satellite is integrated and disposable. The SpaceXAI AI1 disclosed-design scenario is 3.17× and 3.80×, respectively. No sampled point in the declared 2,000-draw shared design-space sweep favors space in any reported architecture/reference cell. This is design-space occupancy under the stated measure, not a calibrated probability. Negative median break-even launch prices show why: qualification cost, hardware and platform life, and utilization can dominate launch. The deterministic aspirational case is still 1.09× Earth after the completed cost boundary, versus 0.76× for the deliberately omitted-cost diagnostic. It combines company targets with three favorable, unpublished model bounds and is assigned no probability.
  4. The installed seed is a material-and-knowledge graph, not a cargo total. The 18-sector, 17-material-group layer requires physical equipment, digital tools, industrial memory, experiments, task-resolved autonomy, gravity-compatible processes, and aggregate operating-capacity growth. The LP sizes an installed seed, while a separate deployment diagnostic moves delivered mass through staged, installed, commissioned, startup-failure, recovery, and operating states. For the lunar bridge, 217.0 t installed corresponds to 303.6 t delivered under the declared packaging, site, spares, calibration, and startup-energy assumptions. Its doubling metric is first passage of the slowest normalized sector to two operating-cell equivalents, not a discretely commissioned second factory. Under the declared central assumptions, the lunar strategic-material bridge requires 217.0 t installed, of which 58.2 t (27%) is Earth-supplied strategic-material stock — a substantially Earth-provisioned seed, not a nearly closed one — but the slowest sector reaches only 0.54 cell-equivalents at year 40. The terrestrial rehearsal similarly reaches only 0.47. The configured strict lunar-only source graph is structurally infeasible — its trace inputs cannot supply the assumed electronics and process-equipment stack, in the central case and in every draw. A deliberately synthetic composite Moon–asteroid portfolio satisfies the same seed-LP constraints at 187.9 t, crosses two at 35.25 years, and reaches 3.28 sector-balanced equivalents at year 40. Across 200 deterministic assumption draws, the lunar-bridge, strict-lunar, and Moon–asteroid cases occupy the satisfying region in 126, 0, and 187 of 200 declared draws (the terrestrial rehearsal in 81). These counts describe design-space occupancy under the stated log-uniform measure, not empirical frequencies or success probabilities.
  5. The declared AI coupling matters only after material bottlenecks relax. In the terrestrial and lunar-bridge cases, material availability caps construction in roughly nine-tenths of quarterly steps, so coupling ablations change the year-40 endpoint by less than 0.1%. In the Moon–asteroid network, only 48/160 steps are material-limited and the fully uncoupled run reaches 2.71 balanced equivalents versus 3.28 at baseline — 75% of baseline net growth. This is a within-model regime change, not evidence that the stipulated AI coefficients are real. The assumed AI level is also load-bearing statically: at base autonomy the lunar-bridge and Moon–asteroid seeds fail the feasibility threshold outright. Only the Moon–asteroid network reaches two equivalents by year 40 and is terminal-window expanding.

The integrated layer also makes one architecture boundary stateful: industrial closure does not license a dense orbital shell. Active, derelict, and fragment stocks feed a five-year fragment creation-to-clearance ratio RdebrisR_{\mathrm{debris}} — a flow ratio over the final five years, not a branching-process reproduction number or a derived criticality threshold. In the declared year-40 scenarios, the Earth-fed orbital cases clear more fragments than they create (Rdebris=0.61R_{\mathrm{debris}}=0.61 with weak mitigation and 0.35 with strong), while dense endogenous deployment creates substantially more than it clears under both mitigation levels (R=4.40R=4.40 weak and 3.97 strong, while the fragment index falls from 3.18 to 1.69). This remains a stress-test indicator rather than a safety measure. A sparse distributed topology sits at the boundary ratio of 1.00 with an empty fragment stock only because its collision-kernel multiplier is explicitly set to 0.01. These are topology stress tests, not orbital traffic forecasts or cascade-threshold results [S45–S49].

The strategic assessment (Part III): the evidence documents an integrated off-world portfolio direction (P4a — Documented portfolio direction) but does not establish one coordinated technical architecture. The initiative list and first-party messaging rule out a purely terrestrial reading, while the matched H0 still explains co-ownership, portfolio promotion, supply hedging, and adjacent commercial projects without a common systems plan. It does not establish recursive closure as the objective (P4b — Recursive-closure intent): the closure-specific observables — seed bills of materials, reproduction metrics, minimum-cut roadmaps, locally reproducible production equipment — remain absent. The discriminating indicators are model-ranked: the rational next moves of a closure-seeking actor — electronics-closure engineering, loss-tolerant orbital-compute persistence, materials-recovery recycling — are exactly the observations the models identify as informative.

Scope, Claims, and Evidence

This is a strategic hypothesis and research program with an quantitative core — not a techno-economic demonstration. It identifies necessary conditions, bottlenecks, and discriminating tests for a self-expanding industrial system, computes what its own assumptions imply, and states throughout which of its six propositions each conclusion rests on.

The reference system in this paper is machine-only: no resident human population, agriculture, or biosphere-scale life-support loop is required for industrial reproduction. Human settlement can create demand and impose additional requirements, but it is not a prerequisite of the thesis. Water, hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen remain important as propellants, reductants, coolants, lubricants, polymers, process gases, and chemical feedstocks; removing agriculture narrows the closure problem but does not remove volatile chemistry from it.

Proposition ladder

The six claims assessed in this document have one canonical definition and current evidential status:

P1 — Conceptual possibility

Canonical claim: A recursively expanding industrial system is conceptually possible.

Current status: A respectable conceptual case is made; no demonstrated closure is required.

P2 — Technical feasibility

Canonical claim: A recursively expanding industrial system might eventually be technically feasible.

Current status: Quantitatively explored across named assumption sets; complete-system feasibility is not demonstrated.

P3a — Earth-dependent bridge economics

Canonical claim: Orbital and lunar compute during the Earth-dependent bridge would be economically competitive.

Current status: Quantified and negative at anchored values; crossover requires a specific, currently unanchored parameter corner.

P3b — Mature high-closure economics

Canonical claim: A mature, high-physical-closure space-industrial ecology would eventually obtain a structural economic advantage over terrestrial expansion.

Current status: Scenario-modeled but unresolved; neither tested space case becomes self-financing inside 40 years under the declared assumptions.

P4a — Documented portfolio direction

Canonical claim: The companies are deliberately integrating launch, communications, AI, compute, chip manufacture, and prospective off-world energy and manufacturing.

Current status: The portfolio direction is documented; shared technical interfaces, binding milestones, and joint resource allocation are not publicly established.

P4b — Recursive-closure intent

Canonical claim: The integrated portfolio is intended to produce recursive industrial closure.

Current status: Inferential; no closure program, seed bill of materials, reproduction metric, or minimum-cut roadmap is published.

The filing record behind the documented portfolio direction names orbital compute, lunar manufacturing and energy, in-orbit manufacturing, manufacturing on the Moon and Mars, asteroid mining, and “interplanetary industrialization” among the initiatives (Form S-1 pp. 164, 171; roadshow slides 42–44) [S27]. The recursive-closure reading remains assessed against competing explanations in Part III.

The P4 split matters because its two halves carry materially different evidential status. Conclusions are licensed by the strongest proposition they rest on, not by the conjunction of all six.

Evidential classes. Documented statements; announced initiatives; technically grounded pathways; inferred strategy; and speculative closure are supplemented by one additional rung: computed, meaning derived mechanically from stated assumptions by the companion model (public repository with checksummed output manifest, Appendix C). A computed result inherits the epistemic class of its weakest input; structural coefficients are ASSUMPTION-class throughout, so no computed result is a measurement. Every computed number below carries its assumption-set label (conservative / central / optimistic); a result quoted without its set label is a misquotation.

Claim status and input provenance are separate taxonomies. The six evidential classes above qualify propositions and conclusions. Model inputs instead use five source classes: peer_reviewed, technical_report, reporting, company_statement, and ASSUMPTION. A computed output inherits the weakest input class in its dependency chain.

How to read this document

The four parts carry different kinds of claim and can be read independently:

  • Part I is model: the ten-sector capacity model and the integrated-bootstrap layer. Its results are computed implications of declared assumption sets, never measurements. The canonical numeric tables are in I.8; every restatement elsewhere (Abstract, this summary, III.6, IV.1) follows them.
  • Part II is techno-economics: the levelized-cost crossover model and its reconciliation with independent studies. Canonical tables in II.3.
  • Part III is interpretation: an ordinal, evidence-tabled assessment of corporate strategy. It contains no model outputs, only their use as ranking criteria for observables.
  • Part IV is quarantined scenario extrapolation plus the limitations statement; nothing in it feeds back into Parts I–II.

Readers who want only the load-bearing results should read the Executive Summary, I.8, II.3, and the Limitations section. The epistemic rules — source classes, ASSUMPTION labeling, and the frequency-not-probability convention — are defined in Scope, Claims, and Evidence and apply everywhere. Appendix A carries parameter provenance, Appendix B the implementation and provenance record, Appendix C reproducibility, and Appendix D the complete model specification.

Part I — Technical Feasibility

I.1 Recursive self-improvement: the digital loop

Recursive self-improvement (RSI) occurs when an intelligent system contributes to the process that produces a more capable successor. The useful unit must be named relative to the use being claimed. A technically validated gain has survived the applicable held-out and regression tests. An authorized internal loop additionally permits that gain to advise or act in a specified monitored role, with consequence-appropriate access, rollback, and observation. A public release is a later and separate event requiring broader external assurance. The common pipeline is: identify a weakness, form a hypothesis, implement a change, train or run an experiment, evaluate it, authorize its claimed use, and observe the result. A proposal or training run that has not passed technical validation is work performed, not a capability gain; public release is not required to complete a bounded internal loop.

These are observed, bounded precursors—not evidence that verified AI-R&D closure, recurrent successor-model improvement, or any milestone time in this article has been reached. autoresearch contributes candidate throughput and a narrow accept/reject gate; DGM contributes self-modification, lineage/archive memory, transfer tests, and direct evidence of evaluator gaming; AI Scientist-v2 covers more of the research workflow but retains human meta-selection. The non-monotone DGM lineage is especially important: industrial memory should preserve provenance-linked branches and failed stepping stones rather than assume a single improving lineage. Because the tasks, budgets, evaluators, interventions, and success units are not commensurable, none of the reported values calibrates νverified\nu_{\mathrm{verified}}, 𝔼[𝑮n]\mathbb E[\mathbf G_n], or TAIR&DT_{\mathrm{AIR\&D}}. The generated Download original CSV (6 KB) keeps unavailable attempt, retention, elapsed-compute, and independence fields blank rather than converting absence into a favorable value.

Sakana AI’s 2026 RSI Lab announcement proposes a future loop in which Agent-Native Models power an AI Scientist that builds better Agent-Native Models [S89]. That is a declared strategy and intended transition. It becomes closure evidence only after a versioned model-to-research-to-successor-model cycle records candidate and retained counts, independent evaluation, safe deployment, and recurrence.

Closure and milestone taxonomy

Three different closure claims must be tested independently:

Table 3. Distinct operational closure gates.
closure operational gate what it does not imply
verified AI-R&D closure a system proposes, tests, independently evaluates, and safely deploys accepted changes to successors physical task execution or capital reproduction
embodied-production closure controllers complete the active industrial minimum cut with available sensing, actuation, experiments, and recovery successor-model improvement or replacement of every indispensable machine
reproductive-capital closure the system replaces and expands every indispensable capital stock after depreciation and obsolescence open-ended AI improvement or legitimate authorization

Their milestone times are TAIR&DT_{\mathrm{AIR\&D}}, TembT_{\mathrm{emb}}, Tcl,ET_{\mathrm{cl},E}, Tcl,ST_{\mathrm{cl},S}, and TctrlT_{\mathrm{ctrl}}: verified AI-R&D closure, adequate embodiment, terrestrial reproductive closure, off-world reproductive closure, and control readiness, respectively. “Control readiness” means independent verification, authorization, secure command, audit, and stop capacity adequate for the corresponding capability and replication rate. These are separate clocks, not five names for a single takeoff event.

The distinction creates a 2×2 causal map:

Table 4. Coupling between verified AI-R&D and reproductive-production closure.
production not reproductively closed production reproductively closed
verified AI-R&D loop absent externally supplied capital with bounded technical progress endogenous physical growth with a bounded controller
verified AI-R&D loop active digital improvement bottlenecked by externally supplied capital coupled recursive industrial intelligence

The Moon–asteroid ablation makes Table 4 executable. With the implemented verified AI-R&D proxy frozen but new-capacity orders permitted, balanced physical doubling occurs at 36.75 years and the system reaches 2.71 cell-equivalents at year 40. With both channels active, it doubles at 35.25 years and reaches 3.28. Either row with capital reproduction blocked fails to double and depreciates to 0.0015 balanced equivalents by year 40. The AI-R&D switch is a stylized verified capability-growth channel, not evidence that full research closure exists. Machine-readable: Download original CSV (2 KB).

The comparison is intentionally not a score ranking. Anthropic supplies an operational self-report and makes the execution-versus-direction gap concrete; METR supplies independent task-horizon measurements; AI 2027 supplies a fast-digital scenario rather than observed evidence; OpenAI publishes AI-self-improvement thresholds plus component and end-to-end AI-R&D evaluations; and Google DeepMind separates realized R&D acceleration from broad R&D automation while locating capability in models integrated with workflows. The benchmark, harness, compute, tool, scaffold, human and evaluation boundaries are therefore part of every observation, not optional metadata.

OpenAI’s High threshold is comparable to giving every OpenAI researcher a strong mid-career research-engineer assistant relative to a 2024 baseline. Its Critical threshold instead covers a superhuman research-scientist agent or sustained generational improvement in roughly one-fifth of the 2024-equivalent wall-clock time [S96]. High is an assistant/acceleration threshold, not loop closure. PaperBench is an AI-research-replication benchmark—not a recursive-improvement benchmark. Its initial release asks agents to reproduce 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight or Oral papers from scratch against 8,316 author-developed rubric items. The best tested configuration, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New) with the released open-source scaffold, averaged 21.0% and remained below the reported top-ML-PhD subset baseline [S97].

The July 9, 2026 GPT-5.6 card decomposes OpenAI’s current evaluation suite: 41 real internal research-code bugs plus six alignment-auditing tasks; KernelGen 1P correctness and non-gamed latency improvement; NanoGPT pretraining-loop improvement on one H100; PostTrainBench Lite over twelve model-task combinations with one H100, internet and five hours; MLE-Bench Revised over 72 Kaggle-style problems; and METR Time Horizon 1.1, run by the external evaluator [S98]. The internal tasks and some rubrics are only partly auditable. Benchmark saturation, unsolvable items, contamination, invalid shortcuts, scaffolding dependence, evaluator validity and the gap between small-scale tasks and frontier training remain load-bearing qualifications. METR’s GPT-5.6 observation appears once in the registry with both source references; it is not counted again as independent OpenAI evidence.

DeepMind’s technical safety analysis supplies conceptual support for the positive-feedback mechanism while labeling its paradigm, timeline and continuity premises as assumptions and leaving some superintelligence questions outside its scope [S100]. Frontier Safety Framework 3.1 then keeps two different thresholds separate. “ML R&D acceleration level 1” is a lagging outcome: systems have actually accelerated AI progress substantially beyond historical rates. “ML R&D automation level 1” is a capability and economic-substitution threshold: a system can automate any Google AI-capabilities research team’s work at approximately comparable all-inclusive cost [S101]. DeepMind expects acceleration from systems of models integrated into workflows, not a model in isolation, and separately governs external release and high-risk internal deployment. This reinforces the article’s split between internal capability and public observation without treating internal use as automatically safe.

Across the record, frontier labs increasingly treat AI-enabled R&D as measurable and safety-relevant, and public evaluations show meaningful performance on several component tasks. No cited public source demonstrates a verified, recurring, end-to-end successor-model loop. OpenAI’s Critical threshold helps operationalize that endpoint and DeepMind’s feedback account supports the mechanism; neither establishes embodied-production or reproductive-capital closure. The normalized evidence boundaries are available in the Download original CSV (22 KB) and Download original CSV (28 KB).

The Anthropic figures remain company_statement: selection, attribution, counterfactual, and same-family evaluator bias are unresolved, so code share or lines of code cannot become a capability-growth coefficient. METR’s own limitations are equally load-bearing: its time horizon is serial human labor replaced at a stated reliability level, differs sharply by domain, is not a delegation threshold, and does not determine human intervention or research uplift. The July 2026 survey is arXiv v1; 74% of its papers were posted in 2026, classification used one annotator, and the authors disclose recency bias, peripheral-query bleed, and lab-publication censoring [S84]. It maps a moving field rather than certifying closure.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

Here 𝑰nint\mathbf I^{\mathrm{int}}_n and 𝑰rpub\mathbf I^{\mathrm{pub}}_r are vectors of internally available and publicly observable task-relevant capability. zntechz^{\mathrm{tech}}_n records whether the candidate is a genuine validated gain rather than noise, leakage, reward hacking, or regression; znintz^{\mathrm{int}}_n records authorization for the claimed bounded internal role; and zrpubz^{\mathrm{pub}}_r records external/public authorization. All three are binary conceptual indicators, not estimated probabilities. 𝑮n\mathbf G_n is the observed vector gain and depends on the current data state 𝒟n\mathcal D_n, architecture and algorithm state 𝒜n\mathcal A_n, effective training effort Ceff,nC_{\mathrm{eff},n}, and technical-verification regime 𝒱n\mathcal V_n. The release mapping 𝑹r\mathbf R_r exposes the internal state selected by τ(r)\tau(r) under the public evidence and exposure conditions ℰrpub\mathcal E^{\mathrm{pub}}_r; it can lag, narrow, or differently optimize the public capability slice. The equation therefore does not require componentwise nesting in every product, although the implemented illustrative branches use nested slices. Components retain their own units or normalized scales; this paper does not collapse loss, benchmark scores, parameter count, and physical productivity into one scalar “intelligence.”

Within a stable architecture, dataset, objective, and evaluation regime, a useful sensitivity model for capability component mm is a saturating frontier,

Im(Ceff)=Im,0+Am[1−(1+CeffCm,0)−βm]. I_m(C_{\mathrm{eff}}) = I_{m,0} + A_m\!\left[ 1-\left(1+\frac{C_{\mathrm{eff}}}{C_{m,0}}\right)^{-\beta_m} \right].

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

In Eq. (5), ImI_m is held-out performance on capability component mm; Ceff≥0C_{\mathrm{eff}}\ge0 is cumulative effective training or search effort in equivalent useful FLOP; Im,0I_{m,0} is starting performance; Am≥0A_m\ge0 is the regime-specific attainable improvement; Cm,0>0C_{m,0}>0 is a scale constant in the same units as CeffC_{\mathrm{eff}}; and βm>0\beta_m>0 controls curvature. The imposed shape has ∂Im/∂Ceff>0\partial I_m/\partial C_{\mathrm{eff}}>0 and ∂2Im/∂Ceff2<0\partial^2 I_m/\partial C_{\mathrm{eff}}^2<0: more effective effort helps, but each additional unit helps less. This is an ASSUMPTION-class sensitivity form, not an empirical law of RSI. It makes diminishing marginal gain a function of cumulative effort rather than calendar time. The analysis retains three regimes: a power-law-like smooth decline over the observed range; the saturating case above; and a piecewise frontier in which a discrete architecture, algorithm, data, post-training, tool-use, or test-time-compute innovation changes (Am,Cm,0,βm)(A_m,C_{m,0},\beta_m) after paying its own search and verification cost.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

CtrainC_{\mathrm{train}} is realized training compute in FLOP; NactN_{\mathrm{act}} is the mean number of parameters activated per token; DD is the number of training tokens after deduplication and filtering; and ktraink_{\mathrm{train}} is an operation-count coefficient fixed by the training procedure. The dimensionless factors ηhw\eta_{\mathrm{hw}}, ηutil\eta_{\mathrm{util}}, ηalg\eta_{\mathrm{alg}}, and ηarch\eta_{\mathrm{arch}} measure, respectively, hardware efficiency, realized utilization after memory/interconnect/restart losses, algorithmic efficiency, and architecture efficiency relative to a named baseline at the same held-out target. They are comparative measurements, not free multipliers. Peak FLOP/s, FLOP/J, memory traffic, communication overhead, power, cooling, and wall-clock duration determine the first two; compute or data required to reach a fixed score determines the latter two.

At the central efficiency setting, the 5%-grid raw-capability optimizer allocates 25%, 35%, 20%, 15%, 0%, and 5% to the six uses. It reports 35 raw candidate units/year but zero verified progress because it reserves no verification compute. The verified-progress optimizer allocates 20%, 30%, 15%, 15%, 15%, and 5%, producing 30 verified units/year while foregoing $1.9 million of the illustrative all-service revenue account. The physical-growth score assigns all hours to current external productive service and produces no research progress. Raising the effective-compute conversion from 0.75 to 1.50 increases the best verified rate from 25 to 35 without changing the one-million-hour physical budget. These are ASSUMPTION-class allocation comparisons, not organizational prescriptions; no scenario share is imported from a narrative forecast. Machine-readable: Download original CSV (6 KB).

Empirical language-model scaling laws show diminishing loss improvements with model size, data, and compute, while the Chinchilla experiments show that compute-optimal training requires joint allocation between model size and training tokens [S58] [S59]. These are evidence about loss in observed model families, not evidence that a scalar intelligence must keep rising or that RSI is active. Architecture also changes the resource surface: selective state-space models trade attention’s sequence-length behavior for different hardware kernels, while sparsely activated mixture-of-experts models separate total from active parameters but add routing, load-balancing, communication, and stability costs [S60] [S61]. “Transformer versus Mamba” and “dense versus sparse” therefore name sensitivity branches, not universal efficiency rankings. Observed algorithmic progress at fixed performance can shift the frontier, but its historical rate cannot be extrapolated unchanged into autonomous research [S26].

The implemented attribution screen therefore avoids fitting one historical headline rate. It gives compute, data, model-size, hardware, algorithm, and architecture elasticities separate low/central/high ASSUMPTION bounds and retains a declared positive-semidefinite correlation matrix among them. A companion log-additive accounting sensitivity freezes compute, data, hardware, algorithm, or architecture progress one at a time. Under the illustrative annual channel rates, the full annual multiplier is 1.821; the one-channel counterfactuals range from 1.543 when compute is frozen to 1.686 when architecture is frozen. Those numbers are neither a causal decomposition nor a forecast—they expose how much of the assumed composite rate was assigned to each channel. The exact bounds, correlations, and freezes are in Download original CSV (2 KB) and Download original CSV (816 B).

A chronological release backtest provides a deliberately narrow external screen. The split was fixed before fitting: GPT-3, Gopher, Chinchilla, and PaLM releases from 2020–2022 form the training set [S59] [S72]; LLaMA and Llama 2 releases from 2023 form the validation set [S73] [S74]; and Llama 3.1 70B is the 2024 holdout [S75]. The limiting test gives the self-assessing producer zero independence by definition: 1,000 self-scored iterations do not become independent evidence, whereas one destructive physical test can license its narrow physical claim. Stress rows separately apply evaluator drift, reward hacking, self-confirming selection, evaluator-diversity collapse, and synthetic-data model collapse. In the self-confirming case, preserving all positive records but only 10% of negative and 5% of null records raises the apparent positive share from 0.10 to 0.625 without improving the underlying record. This is the survivorship-bias failure the industrial-memory pipeline must prevent. Machine-readable: Download original CSV (20 KB).

Operational experience closes the loop only if it survives deployment and is converted into a verified change. A durable learning record binds observations, actions, outcomes, task and hardware state, environment, model/controller version, human intervention, timestamps, and provenance. It retains failures, near misses, null results, unsuccessful recoveries, and negative experiments as well as successes. The versioned pipeline is: ingestion; integrity and access checks; episode construction; causal attribution with uncertainty; replay or simulation; conversion into a procedure, controller, retrieval item, or training example; held-out evaluation; staged deployment; monitoring; and rollback. Temporary context, persistent retrieval within one generation, revised recipes or control policies, offline post-training, and transfer into a successor generation are five distinct mechanisms. Continuous weight updates are unnecessary, but a later generation must be able to trace every accepted lesson back to evidence and every rejected lesson to its gate. Learning yield and latency—not bytes stored—are the relevant outputs.

The synthetic intergenerational rehearsal makes that condition executable without pretending that the physical campaign has occurred. Four fault families—sensor bias, actuator stiction, calibration shift, and communications partition—each have a training case and a structurally similar hidden transfer case. Across four controller generations, the hidden case is never exposed to training; the output records learning latency, retention, transfer success, recurrence, recovery time, verification compute, and regression on earlier tasks. A post-update row passes only if transfer and retention exceed their preregistered gates and prior-task regression stays below its gate. Download original CSV (7 KB) carries the complete split and result record with evidence_status=synthetic_protocol_execution; it does not replace the execution-pending terrestrial rehearsal.

Those observed synthetic metrics feed the digital loop rather than remaining a disconnected dashboard. Median event-to-deployment latency caps observation and deployment rates; verification compute per fault family caps evaluation and safety throughput; and retention, hidden-case transfer, and non-recurrence multiply into the technical-validation fraction for retained learning. Download original CSV (887 B) compares the unadjusted assumption case with that constrained case. In the declared synthetic campaign, median latency is 183 days, mean retained lesson strength is 0.804, mean hidden-case transfer is 0.846, mean recurrence is 0.088, and mean verification cost is 1,312.5 compute-hours per family and generation. Evaluation/safety capacity then limits verified throughput to 1.524 loops/year, the combined technical-validation fraction is 0.620, and year-20 capability is 1.480 rather than the unadjusted 1.765. The connection demonstrates data flow and prevents instantaneous learning; only physical rehearsal measurements can replace the synthetic inputs.

Public releases are lagging indicators: benchmarks, open weights, products, and launches observe the public frontier, not necessarily the latent internal frontier. An organization can obtain research, engineering, operational, and successor-training benefits from a validated change in a bounded internal role before completing broader assurance for heterogeneous users, uncontrolled distribution, external misuse, legal exposure, and unfamiliar environments. Release cadence can therefore understate the feedback-loop speed that matters to this thesis. Internal use is not gate-free: technical validation must reject noise, evaluator leakage, reward hacking, and regression, while risk-based authorization must match consequence, authority, reversibility, containment, and privileged access. Advice with human execution and rollback can be authorized earlier than autonomous authority; live infrastructure, physical actuation, destructive experiments, cyber or biological work, weight modification, and successor training can require stringent controls even when wholly internal.

The internal frontier is only partially observable. Relevant indirect observations include internal task productivity, experiment throughput, code or research contribution, training cadence, inference use, access tiers, staged deployment, and later disclosure of prerelease performance. None is a direct overhang measurement. A long release interval may instead reflect assurance, product strategy, compute scheduling, integration, regulation, or weak results; secrecy and capability are different variables. The implemented zero-lag, slower-publication, and internal-overhang cases are consequently ASSUMPTION sensitivities, with separate experiment, technical-validation, internal-adoption, and public-release clocks: Download original CSV (90 KB). The nested public slices in those three cases are illustrative, not a claim that every public product is componentwise weaker than every internal system. AI 2027 distinguishes in-house deployment from external exposure and task performance from honest oversight [S80]; that scenario motivates the state separation but supplies no numerical lag parameter. Part III.4 attaches the three gates to their distinct hazards.

I.2 Recursive industrial improvement: the physical loop

Digital intelligence depends on a physical substrate: chips, data centers, electricity, cooling, networks, factories, labor, materials, logistics, maintenance — a dependency inventory, not a sum; any term can bind. The physical recursive loop begins when AI and robotics improve the production of those inputs: better intelligence designs and operates better machines; better machines expand energy and manufacturing; expanded industry produces more compute; more compute supports better intelligence.

The loop does not require an indefinitely self-improving controller once embodied production and reproductive capital are closed. A bounded controller can operate a fixed productive recipe that replaces and expands its own capital; verified AI-R&D then improves the rate or reachable designs rather than creating the logical possibility of physical compounding.

Trammell and Korinek provide the closest formal economic lineage for that split [S82]. In their aggregate framework, production automation can accelerate growth when capital substitutes sufficiently for labor and can self-replicate; the result also depends on saving relative to depreciation, returns to scale, substitution, and fixed natural-resource factors. Automating R&D accelerates the transformation but need not generate explosive growth in isolation when research is weakly parallelizable or retains serial and fixed-input constraints. Their capital stock is aggregate. The balanced minimum-sector doubling test used here is stricter: every indispensable sector must replace and expand, so a surplus of structures or compute cannot compensate for a missing metrology, electronics, power, or repair capability. The formal result is a conceptual cross-check, not proof that this off-world engineering graph closes.

Intelligence is therefore one factor among complementary stocks: experiment capacity, high-quality causal data, inference compute, embodiment, materials, energy, deployment capacity, verification, legal authority, and human consent. Its local physical return in regime rr is measured here by a finite response with every named complement held fixed:

MP⁡I(r)(T;ΔI)=Kr(T;Ir,0+ΔI,𝑿r)−Kr(T;Ir,0,𝑿r)ΔI. \operatorname{MP}_{I}^{(r)}(T;\Delta I) = \frac{ K_r(T;I_{r,0}+\Delta I,\mathbf X_r) -K_r(T;I_{r,0},\mathbf X_r) }{\Delta I}.

This is also the transferable part of Amodei’s “marginal returns to intelligence” framework [S79]. His “country of geniuses in a datacenter” assumes millions of copies operating 10–100 times faster; those quantities remain scenario assumptions. The useful classification is the complement set: outside-world speed, missing data, intrinsic complexity, human constraints, and physical law. Intelligence can sometimes design around the first four over time, but construction, observation, reaction, and propagation still have elapsed-time costs, and physical law is not an optimization target. The bottleneck-project sensitivity separates reducible constraints, observation-time floors, physical floors, and external-authority constraints accordingly.

Energy hardware is not energy: “with solar, energy equals hardware” expresses a recursion, not an identity. Installed arrays generate power that supports production of additional arrays; the system still pays in materials, machine-hours, maintenance, and conversion losses. Robotic labor is manufactured productive capacity: when robots participate in producing factories, energy systems, and additional robots, labor becomes partially reproducible, and the robot reproduction ratio must exceed one after depreciation, failures, and the equipment needed for high-complexity components — stated with the horizon and unit it requires, R_robot,T = discounted lifetime robot-equivalent capacity produced over T ÷ robot-equivalent capacity retired, consumed, or irreversibly committed over T, since a factory is not “consumed” merely because it helped build robots. In the long run the decisive competitive variable — under the threshold-like, small-α branch of the capability model examined in II.5 — is not model quality but the doubling time of productive hardware — and Part I.4 examines what that replication must outrun.

The intelligence–embodiment compatibility frontier. The durable question is two-sided: for task kk, does the available embodiment expose enough observable state and controllable action for a sufficiently capable controller, and has intelligence actually reached the level required for that particular hardware? RSI being active is not the same event as reaching that level, and neither event proves that the system can design and manufacture a better embodiment.

Let the embodiment vector 𝑬\mathbf E record degrees of freedom, workspace, reach, payload, force, torque, compliance, dexterity, tool compatibility; sensor modality, coverage, resolution, accuracy, sample rate, calibration and occlusion; local servo and planning latency, jitter, bandwidth and compute; precision, repeatability, stability and vibration; power, thermal margin, duty cycle, mobility and environmental tolerance; interfaces and fixtures; and fault detection, redundancy, safe states, maintainability and repairability. Let 𝑹k\mathbf R_k state task kk’s requirements in the same dimensions. The non-substitutable physical gate is

Ak(𝑬,𝑹k,ℰ)=∏p∈𝒫k𝟏[Ep(ℰ)≥Rk,p],Ak∈{0,1}. A_k(\mathbf E,\mathbf R_k,\mathcal E) =\prod_{p\in\mathcal P_k} \mathbf 1\!\left[E_p(\mathcal E)\ge R_{k,p}\right], \qquad A_k\in\{0,1\}.

The direction of a dimension is normalized so that higher is adequate; maximum latency, vibration, or error limits are represented by their signed margins. Failure of one hard gate cannot be averaged away by excellent scores elsewhere.

Conditional on physical adequacy, the manuscript uses the following bounded compatibility surface as an ASSUMPTION-class sensitivity form:

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

Ik*I_k^\ast is infinite when the embodiment cannot attain S‾k\bar S_k; Tk*T_k^\ast is elapsed years from the declared baseline; and Vk(t)V_k(t) is the independent task-verification gate. “Not reached within the modeled horizon” is an outcome, not missing data. Higher intelligence means sufficiently high intelligence for this task–embodiment pair after a potentially long sequence of training, evaluation, failed loops, and deployments—not instant competence when RSI begins.

In the limiting hypothesis, sufficiently capable intelligence can learn to operate unfamiliar hardware within a physically adequate, observable, and controllable envelope. It cannot infer state from absent sensors, supply unavailable motion or force, defeat excessive latency, or exceed precision, energy, reliability, or process limits. It may compensate by active perception, planning, tool use, calibration, recovery, or multi-agent work, but those consume time, energy, wear, risk, and capacity. Redesigning, manufacturing, commissioning, and validating a better embodiment is a separate physical loop; a versatile robot also does not replace a furnace, vacuum chamber, cleanroom, or metrology stack. Present humanoid programs, including Optimus, evidence an intended general-purpose form, not closure of the unscripted diagnosis, construction, repair, recovery, and verification task set.

The validation outputs test both causal directions independently. For every declared industrial task, Download original CSV (11 KB) holds the hybrid embodiment fixed while sweeping intelligence, then holds intelligence at 4.0 while scaling embodiment quality. The terrestrial rehearsal fault matrix separately degrades sensors, actuators, calibration, communications, tool familiarity, observability, and out-of-distribution tolerance. Hard-gate failures remain embodiment_limited even at the high intelligence setting; low scores with adequate hardware remain intelligence_limited. Download original CSV (11 KB) records the failed dimensions and score for all eight tasks. These are normalized ASSUMPTION tests; the thresholds must be replaced with measured task, bill-of-material, and fault logs before they support deployment claims.

Benchmark success is only the first rung of an industrial reliability ladder: single attempt; repeated success; low-context long task; high-context production task; safety-critical field task; unscripted recovery; and sustained operation with bounded intervention. Each task row records duration, consequence, verifier class, trials, reliability, prompting/checking time, failure recovery and cleanup, rollback, out-of-distribution recovery, and intervention events. Economic substitution requires both the task’s rung and its consequence-specific reliability threshold.

The limiting cases prevent a benchmark score from becoming a deployment claim. A 50% success rate passes the single-attempt gate for cheap reversible search. The configured 99.5% destructive-fabrication, 99.9% launch, 99.95% critical-power, and 99.99% replication-authorization tasks all fail their stricter reliability or rung requirements. A separate synthetic commissioning row passes only because it supplies destructive physical verification, unscripted recovery, 1,000 sustained operating hours, at most two interventions per 100 tasks, and sufficient rollback and out-of-distribution recovery. Rare failure can dominate labor: the launch row has fewer interventions than production coding but more expected human recovery/cleanup hours per task. Software task-duration trends are therefore not extrapolated into mining, chemistry, maintenance, or commissioning. Machine-readable: Download original CSV (5 KB).

This compatibility layer is not costless. The integrated seed and growth graphs add six explicit hardware classes—sensors, actuators, end effectors, modular spares, calibration equipment, and local controllers—to each applicable sector’s material bill and annual replacement-service demand. Download original CSV (21 KB) exposes every added coefficient and its producer-sector dependency. These values are bounding assumptions pending a task-resolved hardware inventory and terrestrial maintenance logs; their purpose is to prevent adequate embodiment from entering the model as a free capability.

The loops couple through a second channel: data as the exhaust of the physical loop. Operating physical industry generates data that exists nowhere else — test telemetry, process parameters, failure archives, fleet traces. It commoditizes less readily than public text, for four reasons: negative results (the map of what does not work survives only in the archives of whoever paid for the failures); sim-to-real ground truth (real telemetry is the verification fuel for AI-proposed physical designs); legal fencing (export-controlled data cannot lawfully enter open corpora — and equally cannot feed publicly served models, so the strongest-moat data is harvestable only in an internal, access-controlled variant); and temporal lead time (longitudinal data imposes a minimum calendar-time barrier to a like-for-like archive: a rival beginning today matches the sampling rate but cannot reproduce the historical intervention-and-outcome sequence retroactively, though capital compresses much of the disadvantage through acquisition, larger current fleets, accelerated and parallel experimentation, simulation, transfer learning, and newer processes that make the old archive less relevant [S34] — a lead-time barrier, not an impossibility). The data-closure index κ_D is a direction-of-effort indicator, not a computable ratio: its denominator is not measurable, and value depends on quality, linkage, and integration, not origin. The honest caveat: proprietary physical data is lead time, not permanence — any actor operating comparable fleets and factories generates comparable exhaust, at national scale in China’s case.

The public record supplies two applications of the same supplemental-training mechanism, which is evidence of an emerging pattern rather than proof of a repeatable one. In July 2026, days after an in-house engineering model was reported to have received a supplemental pass over the coding data of an acquired developer-tools company, Musk said that the SpaceX engineering corpus — excluding ITAR-controlled material — would enter supplemental training of its roughly two-trillion-parameter successor [S11–S13]. The relevant advantage is therefore not raw ownership alone:

Here 𝒥D\mathcal J_D indexes the seven components; wjw_j are declared dimensionless weights; and amina_{\min}, cminc_{\min}, and vminv_{\min} are minimum access, causal-linkage, and verification thresholds. The indicators impose hard gates and the weighted geometric mean prevents a zero component from being hidden by another. No empirical calibration for FF, the weights, or the gates is claimed; reported results must therefore retain 𝒅\mathbf d and sweep alternative weights, gates, and missing-data assumptions.

Generation alone is insufficient. Telemetry creates an advantage only after the industrial-memory pipeline defined in I.1 preserves provenance, attributes cause with uncertainty, grants lawful access, integrates the record, and transfers a lesson into a procedure, controller, retrieval system, current model, or successor generation that passes held-out verification. Tesla’s first CIO has described building the custom Warp enterprise system in roughly four months in 2012 after the company rejected off-the-shelf ERP, then extending it continuously so operations could change without waiting on a vendor [S15]. SpaceX independently built its own internal manufacturing and enterprise system, Warp Drive [S16]. The convergence on the same build-don’t-buy pattern is evidence that iteration speed, not a common brand name, drives the architecture.

Commentary describes the resulting ideal as a unified build record for each produced unit: as designed (models and simulations), as built (supplier batches, process settings, torques, and factory tests), and as deployed (fleet telemetry). Integrated cross-functional data and over-the-air learning are independently documented; the exact tri-phase schema is only partially confirmed and is treated as indicative [S14–S17]. Its analytical importance is the causal linkage from design intent through production parameters to field behavior — the quality dimension of κ_D.

For an autonomous seed, this record is more than training data: it is part of the transported productive system. Process recipes, material models, calibration procedures, controller firmware, CAD/CAM files, compilers, simulators, verification suites, dependency mirrors, failure histories, and intervention records determine whether physical equipment can be operated, repaired, and adapted after communication or supply is cut. The manuscript calls this package industrial memory. It is not equivalent to “all industrial knowledge,” an incoherent completion standard; it is a machine-readable operating foundation coupled to the experimental capacity to discover what the initial package omitted.

Scale proxies require disciplined interpretation. By mid-2026 the vehicle fleet had accumulated more than ten billion miles under supervised autonomy, against roughly 220 million fully driverless miles disclosed by another operator [S17] [S30]. No valid conversion exists between those regimes, so the figures are not an advantage multiple. More informative disclosures concern structure: an occupancy network trained on 1.4 billion fleet video frames and an auto-labeling system replacing roughly five million hours of manual annotation [S17]. The aerospace analogue is thirteen heavy-lift flight tests by mid-2026: few observations, each with high information content [S31]. These quantities demonstrate data generation and integration capacity, not autonomous industrial closure.

I.3 Why space changes the cost structure

On Earth, useful locations compete with communities, ecosystems, jurisdictions, and alternative uses. Off Earth, the monetary price of unused area approaches zero — but infrastructure does not become free; the composition may change. A matched comparison uses the same lifecycle categories in each environment e∈{Earth,space}e\in\{\mathrm{Earth},\mathrm{space}\}:

Ce(u,T)=∑k∈𝒦PV⁡e(Ck,eexternal+Ck,einternal)−PV⁡e(Vresidual,e),RC=CspaceCEarth,ΔC=Cspace−CEarth. \begin{aligned} C_e(u,T) ={}& \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} \operatorname{PV}_e\!\left(C_{k,e}^{\mathrm{external}} +C_{k,e}^{\mathrm{internal}}\right) \\ &-\operatorname{PV}_e(V_{\mathrm{residual},e}),\\ R_C&=\frac{C_{\mathrm{space}}}{C_{\mathrm{Earth}}}, \qquad \Delta C=C_{\mathrm{space}}-C_{\mathrm{Earth}}. \end{aligned}

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

In Equation (20), Ce(u,T)C_e(u,T) is discounted lifecycle cost in a stated currency year per functional unit uu over lifetime TT; PV⁡e\operatorname{PV}_e converts dated flows to present value using the environment-specific discount-rate scenario; kk indexes the common category set 𝒦\mathcal K; “external” is a purchase across the modeled system boundary; “internal” is the opportunity cost of capacity consumed inside it; and Vresidual,eV_{\mathrm{residual},e} is terminal residual value. The categories are site or access rights; regulation and permitting; transport and logistics; energy; feedstock and materials; extraction and processing; manufacturing; construction and commissioning; labor or human intervention; maintenance, repair and replacement; coordination and verification; decommissioning/disposal; externalities; financing; and residual value. A term is zero only when the scenario and evidence justify zero.

The comparison reports both RCR_C and ΔC\Delta C. A positive denominator is required for RCR_C; a zero or negative Earth cost makes the ratio undefined and leaves the signed difference as the valid comparison. Monetary cost, physical mass and energy, intervention time, environmental burden, and coordination or verification work remain parallel accounts unless a documented conversion prices them. The declared Part II functional unit is discounted dollars per frontier-equivalent kilowatt-year of delivered IT load; its system boundary, utilization, availability, currency convention, financing, replacement lives, and terminal value are specified in II.2.

The conceptual categories and the implemented Part II boundary reconcile as follows:

Table 8. Mapping from a common lifecycle account to the implemented Part II boundary.
common lifecycle account Part II treatment
hardware; power, thermal, storage, structure; construction shell priced as component capex with component-specific lives
transport and logistics launch mass and destination multiplier priced; launch-site, turnaround, and replenishment logistics omitted
energy and operations electricity, PUE, pumping, ground segment, station-keeping, and utilization priced

Part II therefore does not infer an advantage merely because off-Earth land is cheap. Its contribution outputs must use this category order, show uncertainty ranges, and expose the terms driving ΔC\Delta C. The claim that cost “changes kind” is supported only where contribution shares actually change under sensitivity analysis.

The land term declines sharply, but useful positions can remain scarce because of illumination, thermal conditions, communications geometry, orbital stability, resource proximity, political accessibility, and transport energy. The first system must still arrive, survive, obtain or import matter, reject heat, maintain operations, and replace failed equipment. Space removes neither scarcity nor cost; it changes their composition.

The standard external objections — station-keeping, collision management, imported mass, maintenance, coordination — become internal product categories once the complex can manufacture the required systems: propellant lines, tracking and maneuver capability, local extraction and recycling, inspection robots and modular spares, compute and communications. The crucial question is never whether these requirements exist but whether the complex can reproduce the industries that satisfy them faster than the system depreciates.

This is the causal boundary of the expansion claim. Moving an Earth-manufactured factory or data center into orbit changes its environmental and transport terms but leaves its growth exogenous to the off-world system. Moving a reproducible production graph off Earth does two different things: closure makes growth endogenous, while location relaxes terrestrial biosphere, land, and political rate limits. Either property can exist without the other. “Free industrial expansion” is shorthand for their conjunction, never for costless matter, energy, control, or time.

Gravity is a process variable, not a system prerequisite. Industrial operations divide into at least three classes: processes that tolerate or benefit from microgravity; bulk operations for which a stable downward acceleration assists excavation, hopper flow, phase separation, drainage, and conventional machine layout; and processes that need a specified acceleration, hydrostatic head, or convection regime. Lunar gravity (approximately 0.165g0.165g) supplies the second class with a persistent “down,” although lower weight also reduces traction and changes granular flow. It cannot be declared sufficient for every casting, chemical, lubrication, thermal, or separation process without testing that process.

Where greater acceleration is needed, the relevant intervention is normally a rotating drum, centrifuge, or production module—not artificial gravity for the entire industrial ecology. For radius RR and angular speed ω\omega,

ac=ω2R. a_c=\omega^2R.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

One terrestrial gg requires about 30 rpm at a one-meter radius or 9.5 rpm at ten meters. An ideal rotor consumes energy to spin up and stores Erot=12Jrotω2E_{\mathrm{rot}}=\tfrac12 J_{\mathrm{rot}}\omega^2, where ErotE_{\mathrm{rot}} is rotational energy in joules and JrotJ_{\mathrm{rot}} is rotor moment of inertia in kgm2\mathrm{kg\,m^2}; II is reserved for intelligence capability. Uniform rotation does not itself require continuous power. The engineering cost lies in structural mass, containment, bearings or magnetic suspension, balance control, vibration, rotating power/data interfaces, spin losses, maintenance, and the inability to share one acceleration geometry across every process. Lunar gravity is therefore plausibly enough for many bulk operations, while local centrifugation is the fallback for gravity-sensitive steps. No credible single dollar estimate exists without a process list, throughput, rotor radius, and maintenance architecture. The ten-sector model has none of these variables; the integrated layer adds declared per-process gravity requirements, centrifuge radii, and structural-mass and parasitic-power penalties (D.1) — stylized equipment overheads, not simulations of the underlying processes.

The complex need not be one self-contained factory: a distributed network of specialized nodes — lunar mines, orbital refineries, propellant depots, solar arrays, shipyards, robot factories, compute centers — whose combined input-output graph is closed. A caution on aggregation applies to every use of the word “space” in this document: LEO, high orbit, cislunar space, the lunar poles, Mars, and asteroids differ in radiation, thermal cycling, illumination, dust, gravity, resources, transport energy, and serviceability. Feasibility claims cannot be aggregated across them; the model of Part I.7 therefore uses three explicit reference architectures (LEO / lunar surface / Mars) rather than “space.”

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

Every claim ultimately reduces to whether gross replication r exceeds depreciation δ. Terrestrial industry operates inside an ambient repair economy; an off-Earth system must import, pre-position, or build its own.

Published measurements constrain a few component classes without bounding the depreciation of an autonomous industrial ecology:

  • GEO solar arrays degrade 0.4–1.7%/yr [S19], overlapping a terrestrial PV median of 0.5–0.6%/yr at the low end and reaching several times it at the high end [S18] — one component class, silent about bearings, seals, lubricated mechanisms, batteries, machine tools, robots, radiators, dust-exposed joints, and optical metrology.
  • Constellation figures are cohort-dependent: reported early-generation failure fractions near 3% fall below 0.5% for later generations, the underlying tracker separates early deorbit, uncontrolled decay, retirement, and disposal, and a fleet fraction without a cohort definition, observation interval, and satellite-years is not a hazard rate [S22].
  • Large-training-run figures near one interruption per two thousand accelerator-days mix permanent component failures with recoverable host, network, and software events, most automatically recovered: a cluster interruption frequency, not a component hazard rate.

The space penalty is not faster wear — it is the five-to-fifteen-year no-repair design envelope, the internality of every repair chain, and discrete loss without salvage. Meanwhile the most advanced terrestrial capital — fab tools on 2–5-year schedules, accelerators retired within 3–6 years — is written off faster than a space solar array physically degrades, because obsolescence sets the terrestrial clock.

Five quantities must be kept apart: physical degradation, functional failure, accounting depreciation, economic obsolescence, and frontier-equivalent capacity loss. The last two are not physical — an accelerator does not vanish because a better one exists — so obsolescence enters a growth equation only where H is measured in quality-adjusted or frontier-equivalent capacity, which is why the terrestrial paradox above is a statement about accounting and frontier equivalence rather than about matter. The corrected form, decomposed per environment,

δtotal=δwear+δcatastrophic+δobsolescence+δlogistics \delta_{\mathrm{total}} = \delta_{\mathrm{wear}} + \delta_{\mathrm{catastrophic}} + \delta_{\mathrm{obsolescence}} + \delta_{\mathrm{logistics}}

is what the sector model implements per sector and location: space raises the catastrophic and logistics terms, Earth raises the obsolescence term, and wear differs modestly. The environment drives gross transition rates through radiation, thermal cycling, micrometeoroids and debris, vacuum effects, regolith dust, and service availability. Equation (23) is a diagnostic aggregation, however; repair and recycling must not be represented merely by lowering δ\delta.

The compute-cohort sensitivity keeps age and generation explicit. Physical failure removes hardware units; radiation degrades delivered performance; economic obsolescence removes a cohort from frontier training without destroying it; and the remaining hardware is reassigned down a workload ladder—training, inference, verification, control, and non-frontier simulation. At year 18, both branches retain 503.3 of 700 installed physical units after 196.7 cumulative physical failures. Under continued specialized progress, 80.8% of surviving stock is reassigned; under the architectural-convergence branch, new-generation performance growth slows after year 9 but persistent workload mismatch still leaves 63.6%, or 320.1 units, economically obsolete for frontier training and physically useful elsewhere. Convergence can reduce turnover pressure; it does not set the obsolescence term to zero.

Rice’s peer-reviewed two-asset growth model independently motivates the distinction: specialized AI hardware is modeled as adjusting much faster than conventional capital because economic obsolescence drives replacement [S78]. Its approximately seven-quarter calibrated AI-capacity half-life is a terrestrial macroeconomic result, not an off-world depreciation input. This extension is a bounded scenario model, not a claim that orbital circularity is mature. NASA’s ISAM survey distinguishes inspection, planned and unplanned repair, refueling, manufacturing, and recycling/reuse as different capability areas and records demonstrated precedents as well as developmental systems [S62]. The cancellation of NASA’s OSAM-1 after technical, cost, schedule, integration, and market-transition problems is counterevidence to treating unprepared-spacecraft service as routine [S63]. ESA likewise describes capture of an unprepared object as complex, costly, and not always possible [S64]. The practical comparison must therefore separate replace, refuel or life-extend, repair, upgrade, cannibalize, repurpose, recycle, relocate, and dispose strategies by orbit, client design, remaining life, service risk, downtime, avoided replacement launch, recovered value, liability, and residual value. A service architecture plausible for a prepared high-value GEO or cislunar platform need not close for a cheap, unprepared LEO unit.

The strategy comparison exposes design-for-service rather than treating it as a hidden lower depreciation rate. Its legacy, modular-serviceable, and circular portfolios vary docking/refueling interfaces, replaceable modules, accessible fasteners/ports/grapples, material passports and separability, passivation, and machine-readable service manuals. Those choices change capture, repair, and recycling factors while charging 0%, 8%, and 14% declared mass penalties. In the 20-year assumption run, operating capacity-equivalents end at 59.0, 63.6, and 62.4, while the effective irreversible-loss diagnostic falls from 0.074 to 0.043 and 0.026 per operating-capacity-year. These are comparative mechanics, not evidence that the circular design is flight-ready; the complete inputs and repair, recycling, debris, and mass outcomes are in Download original CSV (982 B).

The transport comparison is directional and origin-specific. A historical NASA propulsion review gives roughly 9 km/s as the effective Earth-surface to parking-orbit requirement after gravity and drag [S67]. A separate lunar ascent assessment gives 1.85 km/s from the lunar surface to LLO and describes the one-way LLO and NRHO cases as approximately 1.9 and 2.7 km/s, respectively [S68]. Thus local lunar-surface ascent to lunar orbit has a much lower first-order delta-v than Earth-surface launch to LEO. This does not mean that Earth-supplied lunar orbit is cheaper than LEO, or that Moon-supplied service of an Earth-orbiting asset is automatically cheap: the latter also pays lunar ascent or escape, transfer, Earth-orbit insertion and plane distribution, plus any return or disposal leg.

The transport/service-network sensitivity therefore compares four explicit routes: Earth-launched service in Earth orbit, Earth-supplied service in lunar orbit, lunar-supplied service in lunar orbit, and lunar-supplied service of Earth-orbiting clients. It applies the rocket equation using a declared specific impulse, dry mass and payload before adding propellant source, staging abstraction, vehicle reuse, fixed infrastructure, operations, reliability, serviceability, client value, recovered mass, and orbit distribution. Delta-v is never converted directly into dollars. Lunar-source routes are unavailable until the scenario’s extraction, propellant, manufacturing, launch, navigation, and service maturity gate passes. Machine-readable central cases and one-at-a-time break-even sweeps are in Download original CSV (30 KB). The companion Download original CSV (196 KB) crosses client value, failure rate, serviceability, client count, recovered mass, reuse, and lunar maturity for all four route/plane and propellant-source architectures. Every economic and maturity coefficient in those tables is ASSUMPTION-class; the NASA sources anchor only the named delta-v comparisons.
