Threshold observations that would move Appendix A: a demonstrated ISRU plant above ~50% full-system materials closure; audited robot production figures; an independent satellite-reliability audit reporting cohort-specific failures per satellite-year, separated from retirements and planned disposals (an aggregate ~2.5–3% early-cohort fleet fraction is not a general hazard rate and is not the right comparison); and any traceable datum on off-world-producible electronics tiers — the strategic-material-gap anchor this document flags as its highest-value currently parameterized missing measurement. The thesis weakens if humanoid robotics remains economically narrow, advanced manufacturing cannot be localized, launch costs stop declining, closure requires a permanently growing Earth supply chain, verification costs rise faster than capacity — or if Terafab devolves into design-and-packaging dependent on external front-end fabrication, which would reopen the fabrication term entirely.

III.6 Refined complete thesis

The coherent end state remains a recursively self-expanding space industrial ecology. Reusable rockets transport an initial seed. AI supplies scientific, engineering, and coordinating intelligence. Robots provide scalable physical labor. Local energy systems supply power. Mining and refining convert extraterrestrial matter into industrial feedstocks. Automated factories produce structures, machines, robots, transport vehicles, energy systems, and — if the electronics tier can close — compute. Communications integrate specialized nodes into one economic and operational network.

The network first reduces Earth dependence, then reaches self-sustenance, and finally produces net additional capacity. At high closure, station-keeping, collision management, maintenance, transport, and coordination remain real requirements; they are supplied by industries inside the network rather than purchased as externally scarce services.

Matter, energy, intelligence, and elapsed construction time become expanding productive capacity only through the delayed, gated transitions in Equation (3).

Recursive self-improvement is therefore not limited to software. Intelligence improves the machinery and institutions that create intelligence; the industrial substrate returns energy, compute, data, experimentation, and physical agency to the intelligence layer. The ultimate product is an industrial system capable of producing more of itself.

This end state is coupled but non-unitary. Verified AI-R&D, embodied production, and reproductive capital are distinct closure tests. A system may improve successors without reproducing its physical substrate, or reproduce capital under a bounded controller without automating AI research. Their conjunction is the strongest acceleration branch, while the achieved system rate remains bounded by the slowest complementary stock and by authorized verification throughput. Off-Earth resources change the long-run material and siting envelope only after the bridge to reproductive closure; location and intelligence alone do not establish recursion.

The marginal product of intelligence is consequently regime-specific rather than globally positive by definition. The finite-response diagnostic is near zero in the two material-starved cases and positive after the declared source network relaxes supply. Intelligence can propose experimental methods, equipment designs, and schedules; those changes enter capacity only after a funded productive pathway, construction lag, verification, and applicable authorization. Reaction and propagation floors, absent observations, heat rejection, and decisions held by external legal authorities remain explicit constraints rather than presumed targets of optimization.

The precise formulation is conditional and model-separated. The evidence documents deliberate integrated space–AI–industrial direction (P4a — Documented portfolio direction), but neither a shared technical architecture nor an intended transition to recursive closure (P4b — Recursive-closure intent). The ten-sector industrial model finds expansion under some assumption sets and failure under others, with electronics and feedstock dependencies localized by architecture. The 18-sector integrated-bootstrap model represents the complete intelligence–industry loop, seed bill of material, source network, and aggregate operating-capacity growth; it finds the lunar strategic-material bridge and the synthetic Moon–asteroid scenario LP-feasible under central assumptions and the configured strict lunar source graph structurally infeasible. Because every structural coefficient is declared rather than measured, that is an executable hypothesis, not evidence that the complete recursion can be built. The comparative-economics model finds the Earth-dependent bridge uneconomic at anchored values and does not price the mature high-closure ecology. Capability accumulation is observed; positive off-world industrial reproduction and a unified closure strategy are not.

Equation (3) is the article’s compact causal system; this section does not introduce a second loop definition. The ten-sector model operationalizes the productive-capacity update as the lexicographic maximin allocation of Part I.7 (with repair, recycling, stockpiles, and imports) and decomposes environmental depreciation by sector. The integrated layer supplies first stylized response functions: installed compute drives verified intelligence through a saturating gain law; intelligence raises task autonomy and industrial productivity; and operating cells manufacture additional compute only after construction and commissioning lags. Constant-rate Earth-fed deployment is run beside it as the counterfactual. These functions are executable and swept, but their coefficients are ASSUMPTION-class and they omit many algorithmic-regime, hardware-node, and coordination details. The model therefore tests the consequences of a coupling law; it does not measure that law or establish takeoff, subject also to the speed caveat of II.5. The coupling ablations show that in the material-starved terrestrial and lunar-bridge cases, removing the dynamic coupling changes almost nothing; in the stipulated Moon–asteroid network it reduces year-40 net balanced growth by about 46%. The declared f and h therefore become operative only after the source vector relaxes material supply, while the starting AI level also matters through seed feasibility (I.8). This is a regime implication of assumed coefficients, not evidence that the coupling exists at the stipulated strength.

What the thesis does not claim

  • It does not establish that the companies are managed under one confidential master plan; III.3 assesses the public evidence.
  • It does not imply that energy, matter, infrastructure, coordination, or opportunity cost become literally free.
  • It does not assume intelligence automatically solves semiconductor fabrication, reliability, verification, governance, or safety.
  • It does not claim that the degrees of freedom of a current humanoid robot demonstrate unscripted industrial autonomy; embodied task coverage, recovery, and verification remain unmeasured requirements.
  • It does not require human settlement, agriculture, or a closed biosphere for the reference machine ecology, nor does it claim humans could never be present. A crewed architecture is a larger closure problem than the one modeled here.
  • It does not require every industrial node to be self-contained; closure can exist at network level.
  • It does not require uninterrupted exponential growth; the system can move through bottleneck-limited regimes and can double before later losing viability.
  • It does not claim Terafab will achieve viable yields or off-world fabrication closure; it is a declared terrestrial attempt whose implementation remains unsettled.
  • It does not claim a slow takeoff is certain; the physical-path thesis is conditional on the slow-to-medium branch in II.5.
  • It does not claim that closure is imminent, that model frequencies are empirical probabilities, or that space compute is economical today.

Part IV — Conclusion, and Speculative Terminal Scenarios

IV.1 The defensible core, restated with numbers attached

Two constraints, two rate comparisons, one passage. Externally induced supply expansion competes with internally controlled reproduction, while the operating envelope compares terrestrial social and infrastructure costs with off-world transport, reliability, and closure costs. Neither comparison is escaped by terminology; both remain conditional on surviving the bridge. The bridge’s failure mode is specific: hold electronics-class stockpiles against shelf life, and reach local production of some electronics tier before the import ramp decays. The causal core is also narrower than a single coupled-loop slogan: reproductive-capital closure can generate endogenous physical growth with a bounded controller, while verified AI-R&D closure can accelerate design without creating physical reproduction. In the central Moon–asteroid ablation, the bounded-controller branch still doubles at 36.75 years; the fully coupled branch reaches the same threshold at 35.25 years. The strongest acceleration case combines both loops, but neither loop defines the other. The defensible core conclusion stops here, with its conditionals quantified: if industrial closure becomes sufficiently high across every indispensable sector (Part I’s bottleneck is architecture-specific: capture/mining dominates LEO, electronics dominates the Moon, and electronics and power co-bind on Mars) and terrestrial expansion costs rise faster than off-world deployment costs (Part II says: not at anchored values; only in the qualification/life/utilization corner at target-class launch prices), then some large-scale industrial and computational activity may migrate off Earth. Everything beyond that sentence is scenario.

QUARANTINE NOTICE. Sections IV.2–IV.4 are scenario-class: internally consistent extrapolation, not established result. Nothing in them feeds back into Parts I–II inputs. Each scenario carries a model check — usually a constraint, not support.

IV.2 After convergence: deployment as the terminal regime

At some point the marginal value of further design improvement falls below the marginal value of another deployed node — architectural convergence. Past it, intelligence behaves as a commodity produced by infrastructure — heuristically, throughput ~ deployed energy × physical efficiency, a relation that omits memory, interconnect, utilization, data, reliability, verification, latency, workload composition, and fabrication yield. Efficiency is floor-bounded (Landauer, with reversible logic the stated exception); scale plausibly becomes the dominant marginal variable rather than the only one; scale means energy; energy means collector area; and collector area is not bounded by a planetary surface off Earth. It remains bounded — by matter, transport, orbital geometry, heat transport, collision risk, maintenance, and control, and per the published cluster analysis by the quadratic scaling of satellite count with cluster radius and by mutual occlusion of rejected infrared between closely flown spacecraft [S32]. The ceilings-and-rates argument is retained in sensitivity form: the waste-heat ceiling sits perhaps two orders above current civilizational energy use, the thermodynamic floor several orders below current efficiency, and the ~3×/yr algorithmic-efficiency figure [S26] measures compute-for-fixed-language-performance only. Under sustained compounding, distances that look like centuries become decades — whether the compounding is sustained is precisely what is unknown.

The two regimes can be stated as marginal cost curves. On Earth, the marginal cost of the n-th node can rise as the operator bids up land, congests grids, and encounters political and thermal limits. In space, after closure, the marginal cost can fall through learning and self-replication. One curve rises and the other falls; their crossover is the migration point, and it moves earlier as launch cost declines, closure improves, equipment life lengthens, or qualification premiums fall. Part II shows that the curves do not cross at the anchored bridge-economy values.

Model check. The cost-curve claim — Earth’s marginal node rises with n, space’s falls with n after closure — is the crossover surface, and at anchored values the curves do not cross. The scenario needs three demanding unanchored conditions: rad-tolerance at commodity cost (the strongest current data supports five-year TID survivability but leaves system reliability — SEE, training workloads, thermal, whole-spacecraft — unresolved [S32]), service life nearer 15 years than 5, and target-class launch or closure substituting for launch. The collector-area arithmetic is not the disputed part; the three demanding unanchored conditions are where the scenario lives.

Two conditions attach. Demand saturation: if the set of tasks worth computing is bounded, demand saturates and the argument that space is the only arena permitting unbounded deployment loses its motivation [S34]. The physical ceilings bound how cheaply computation can be done; a demand ceiling would bound how much is wanted — the more decisive and less examined of the two. The non-saturation branch has a canonical published statement [S35] and no resolution; the scenario is conditional on it.

The demand sensitivity therefore includes both cases rather than treating non-saturation as a natural law. With identical compute supply growing 20% per year, the illustrative non-saturating branch demands 86.74 units at year 20 against 38.34 available, whereas bounded valuable demand approaches its six-unit ceiling and uses 5.94. A separate bounded branch directs 70% of used compute to humanitarian applications before year 8, compared with 15% in the industrial-priority branch. These allocation shares are normative ASSUMPTION inputs, not forecasts or welfare optima. Machine-readable: Download original CSV (2 KB) and Download original CSV (24 KB).

The upgrade asymmetry, narrowed: software-layer improvements propagate to deployed compute at near-zero marginal cost, but hardware-dependent gains require replacement or retrofit — silicon is not upgraded in place. The model consequence: the space-electronics obsolescence term would shrink after convergence only for its software-limited share.

IV.3 Paradigm shifts: delay, alteration, or prevention

Catch-up time (a new paradigm must beat the incumbent plus decades of compounded process learning, still improving as the newcomer matures) and finiteness (irreversible-computation paradigms climb toward the same ceiling; reversible computing is the stated exception) bound the leapfrog objection. Exposure is concentrated in fabrication on 10–20-year horizons; energy, labor, transport, and materials are less paradigm-sensitive — substantially reusable, not immune. The fleet self-insures through its own 3–6-year depreciation; the fab carries the stranding risk — the penalty of taking the lead.

General-purpose robotic manufacturing is a partial hedge because it is the industry that builds industries: after a paradigm shift, the cheapest retrofitter may be the actor able to build the next fab faster than a rival builds its first. The corresponding strategy is to verticalize the less paradigm-sensitive layers aggressively, preserve hardware generality and retooling capacity at the paradigm-specific layer, and track retooling speed alongside doubling time. The model check below shows that this hedge must be pre-positioned; it cannot be improvised after a catastrophic electronics loss.

Model check. The paradigm-sensitivity split maps onto the model’s sector structure: a shift perturbs the electronics column of the requirement matrix and the fab layer behind the vitamin imports — exactly the sector already identified as binding in the relevant architectures. Machine tools and robotics are necessary retooling capabilities, but all eight modeled physical production sectors are knockout-indispensable; the knockout experiment does not show that those two are uniquely more strategically valuable. Retooling speed is a computed output (cutsets.retooling_time), and it hardens this scenario’s central risk into a result: destroying 90% of the electronics or machine-tools sector at any point on the central trajectory is model-fatal — a defined, horizon-relative label: worst-case growth has not returned positive within the tested 20-year post-knockout window while the unknocked counterfactual’s stays positive, under both the myopic and receding-horizon allocators, and at optimistic values too. The computation tests a 20-year horizon under the stated deterministic configuration; it establishes no recovery within that window, not permanent impossibility — a longer horizon, resumed imports, altered plant design, larger initial surplus, or a lower knock fraction could change the outcome and are unswept. The mechanism is the electronics strategic-material gap: at electronics q-scale 0.10–0.30, replacement local capacity is a multi-decade-payback asset no plausible planning horizon rebuilds from current output. Only power stranding under optimistic values is a finite delay (~27 years lost). Conditional implication: within this scenario class, a paradigm shift that obsoletes the local electronics tier removes the self-expansion margin for at least a two-decade window unless Earth imports resume — so the leapfrog hedge must be pre-positioned (hardware generality, retooling-ready lines, retained umbilical capacity), because post-shift rebuild from inside the complex is not a path the model offers within any tested horizon. Caveats: deterministic values, 90% single-sector knockout, maximin allocation family, 20-year window; surplus-pinning (stage 3), knock-fraction sweeps, and longer-horizon recovery tests remain open follow-ups.

IV.4 The alternative telos, and the properly conditional close

One reading of the same physics reaches this document’s destination from opposite values: Earth is not a constrained platform to escape but a uniquely valuable biosphere to protect — zone the planet for habitation, site heavy industry and compute where there is no ecology to disturb [S34]. Independent corroboration of the operating-wall mechanism comes from the same quarter: data-center siting is politically contested over electricity, water, and land. The physical argument is common to both readings; only the telos differs — and this decouples P3 from P4: the migration case can be made without any claim about one company’s intentions.

Off-world expansion is also not the unique high-value use of advanced intelligence. Amodei’s explicitly non-space vision prioritizes health, poverty reduction, peace, governance, and human meaning [S79]. That countercase prevents infrastructure scale from silently becoming a welfare objective. Space can offer a long-horizon option for relocating harmful activity, expanding physical capacity, and increasing resilience; whether it dominates direct humanitarian uses is an allocation question this article does not resolve.

That telos requires three separate welfare-relevant accounts rather than one “activity moved to space” total:

The observed portfolio is consistent with an economic gradient toward greater integration — discovery until convergence, deployment after it, with space as one plausible arena under a demanding set of priced crossover conditions. Present evidence does not establish that recursive off-world industrial closure is the governing objective of the companies described in Part III. The executable model says that recursion is feasible only under assumptions that are currently choices rather than measurements; the economics point to Earth at every anchored value; and the observations that would change either conclusion are named, ranked, and observable.

The portfolio audit sharpens that boundary into minimum cuts rather than a coverage percentage. Public evidence is deepest in operating terrestrial power, manufacturing, transport, electronics integration, maintenance, and compute, but no modeled sector is off-world reproductively closed. The decisive disclosed gaps are reproduction and calibration of semiconductor process equipment/metrology; qualified local source lots, species-level chemistry, gases, resists, optics, bearings, and material grades; local production of electronics and industrial parent tools; and an off-world repair, verification, spares, and transport-fleet reproduction chain.

Closing 17 partially adjacent rows while leaving any one indispensable parent-tool chain open still leaves the system dependent. That dependency-aware result—not “12 of 18” or any implied percentage—is the relevant conclusion.

Limitations and claim boundary

The most robust outputs are structural within the implemented model: balanced doubling is unit-invariant; the three-stage allocator has a unique state transition; realized endpoints include same-step shocks; recoverable scrap cannot exceed loss-specific retirement; and Part II is exactly affine in launch price. Architecture comparisons, endpoint definitions, and regeneration from fixed seeds are also auditable.

The substantive conclusions remain assumption-conditioned. In the ten-sector model, the requirement matrix, homogeneous electronics-closure multiplier, repair and recovery efficiencies, stockpiles, shock process, import profile, and finite capture reservoir are not measured as a coupled industrial system. Its scalar-anchor screen does not rank structural matrix uncertainty, interactions, policy families, or all environments, and its LEO model has neither an endogenous debris stock nor a depleted capture reservoir.

The integrated layer adds a material-category-by-sector bill of materials, source yields, Earth–Moon–orbit–asteroid transfer arcs, seed-mass and composition-changing Pareto searches, a decomposed knowledge package, observable autonomy gates, process-specific environment profiles, construction and transport lags, cohort-resolved commissioning and yield ramps, architecture-specific viable floors, independent sector allocation, explicit repair, finite orbital feed, and shell-resolved debris. A separate delivery diagnostic distinguishes delivered, staged, installed, commissioned, failed, recovered, and operating seed states. These are model features, not validated factories. Their bills of material, recoverable yields, source throughput, autonomy/productivity gains, lag/ramp/repair coefficients, intervention budget, source portfolio, transfer capacities, environment responses, and collision kernels are declared assumptions. The seed is minimum-mass only inside the enumerated architecture and design alternatives. Seventeen material categories do not resolve mineralogy, alloying routes, contamination, process chemistry, purity ladders, tool wear, quality yield, or every consumable. The electronics tiers remain aggregates rather than fabs and tool chains. Documented elemental occurrence is not a grade distribution, recoverable reserve, refining yield, or accessible asteroid portfolio. The process-closure acceptance contract in params/process_closure_requirements.yaml makes the missing graph explicit: source lots, species, unit processes, grades, critical parts, parent tools, transport legs, waste routes, evidence records, and eight binary gates. The generated Download original CSV (7 KB) remains wholly evidence_pending; the contract does not itself supply those nodes or data. The associated bundle evaluator rejects graphs that omit a grade, critical part family, process stage, evidence hash, or independently witnessed gate.

The terrestrial rehearsal in I.9 remains a proposed validation protocol, not an accomplished demonstration; its computed scenario is a requirements case, not an experiment. Its machine-validated event and acceptance contract is published in params/rehearsal_protocol.yaml, with the unexecuted public matrix in Download original CSV (8 KB). The evidence-bundle evaluator likewise refuses a result unless every event type and injected fault, archive and auditor hash, witnessed gate, and parameter-replacement record is present. Environment profiles change throughput, yield, power, depreciation, and binding rows, but their multipliers do not simulate granular mechanics, convection, melt behavior, vacuum welding, abrasive dust, radiation damage, traction, or thermal-cycle physics. The compute–intelligence loop remains phenomenological even though its gates are expressed as observable task completion, intervention, diagnosis, verification, engineering-cycle, yield, repair-success, and recovery quantities. The shell model is a stress model, not a conjunction-assessment or validated traffic simulation.

Part II includes communications and ground-network capex, spacecraft-bus functions, program NRE, insurance, spectrum/regulatory cost, disposal, residual value, thermal margins, workload boundaries, and separate financing. Serviceability remains a scenario rather than an observed property. A symmetric dynamic economics diagnostic couples technical space capacity and its construction, transfer, and intervention demand to the same investment, financing, learning, depreciation, regulatory-delay, and market mechanics used for Earth. Its coefficients are assumption-class and neither tested space case self-finances inside 40 years, so P3b — Mature high-closure economics remains unresolved rather than inferred from physical compounding. The claim-level provenance audit classifies reporting-derived Part II intervals as ASSUMPTION wherever no source directly supports the modeled endpoints and transformation. Every remaining non-ASSUMPTION anchor resolves through params/claim_provenance.yaml to an exact locator, extracted value, units, transformation, and persistent identifier; the generated public table is Download original CSV (40 KB). This makes the evidence boundary auditable, but it does not empirically calibrate the wide assumption ranges. The economic-calibration contract in params/economic_calibration.yaml defines architecture-specific evidence, equal-workload fields, correlated fitting groups, audited dated cash flows, chronological holdout validation, and the promotion rule. Its public readiness table is entirely data_pending; P3b — Mature high-closure economics remains empirically open. Its bundle evaluator requires all evidence packages, correlated fits, holdouts, cash-flow event types, immutable hashes, and reviewed parameter decisions; point estimates alone cannot satisfy it. Finally, the Part III strategy assessment is ordinal and observational: corporate filings and statements establish declared initiatives, not an intent to achieve recursive closure. No result in this paper is a forecast or an empirical probability of success.

Appendix A: Parameter Anchors

The authoritative, machine-readable anchor set is params/anchors.yaml [S28]; every generated report carries a per-run provenance table. Ranges reflect genuine disagreement across sources; values are anchors, not precision claims. The discipline of normalizing quantities by type and never averaging rate quantities into one “r” is implemented in code (delta.py) rather than prose. Rows marked (context) are documentary quantities cited for interpretation only: they are not wired model inputs and have no YAML entry. Every other row resolves from the YAML, and source classes use only the five input-source classes defined in Scope, Claims, and Evidence.

Claim-level provenance contract. params/claim_provenance.yaml records author or organization, title, date, page/table/section, permanent URL, DOI or content-hashed repository snapshot, extracted value, units, transformation, source class, and verification status for every non-ASSUMPTION anchor. The same register pins the load-bearing [S27] strategy claims to SEC pages or roadshow slides. A test rejects missing records, endpoint drift, source-class drift, collective [S36] support for a non-assumption anchor, and unpinned [S27] claims. The deterministic public render is Download original CSV (40 KB). Ranges whose exact endpoints remain analyst-constructed are explicitly ASSUMPTION, even when reporting or technical literature provides contextual bounds.

A.7 Provisional hiring-sweep note — not an evidence-table item

A July 2026 search across 1,170 open OpenAI and Anthropic postings found multiple roles explicitly concerned with software-RSI preparation and measurement, including early-warning metrics, recursive-self-improvement preparation, chip-design reinforcement learning, and long-horizon training environments. The same search found no roles in fabrication, packaging/test, materials, or production-equipment reproduction. This is a provisional negative-search observation, not evidence of capability or a model input. Its value depends on the unpublished search vocabulary, deduplication rules, per-lab counts, and stability of a changing jobs corpus. The working snapshot is docs/transcripts/lab-job-listings-2026-07-26.md; it should not enter the main evidence table until a public dated audit artifact exists.

Appendix B: Implementation and Provenance

The executable release combines the ten-sector capacity model, the comparative economics model, and an 18-sector, 17-material integrated-bootstrap layer. The integrated layer includes material-category-resolved bills of material, explicit source and transfer arcs, minimum-mass seed sizing, autonomy and intervention constraints, process-environment effects, construction and commissioning dynamics, compute–intelligence–productivity coupling, tiered electronics, finite shell mass, debris dynamics, symmetric economics, and composition-changing robust-seed searches.

Central and 200-draw deterministic assumption-ensemble results are reported in Part I.8 and regenerate from rsi-run-integrated. The release includes sector-resolved cohort dynamics, independent allocation and repair, delivered- seed deployment, observable autonomy and outage regimes, policy and structural sweeps, terminal-window diagnostics, import-stock resolution, coupling ablations, an oversize frontier, and a quantified strict-lunar infeasibility certificate. All remain assumption-conditioned structures pending empirical calibration.

Machine-validated contracts define the still-missing evidence for process-feasible closure, the physical Stage-0 rehearsal, and economic calibration. Their templates are deliberately non-passing: completed bundles must bind every referenced digest to a verified file, and success states must satisfy the underlying fault, holdout, review, and graph-consistency rules. Venue-specific paper drafts and submission contracts are included, but final source/style review, live-portal checks, author-controlled declarations, immutable release coordinates, and submission approval remain pending.

Every generated result is reproducible from the declared configuration, code, and deterministic seeds. outputs/MANIFEST.md binds the canonical manuscript, HTML, source/configuration files, and generated artifacts; outputs/integrated/MANIFEST.md additionally records the integrated run inputs and outputs. No model output is presented as a measurement, empirical probability, engineering estimate, or forecast.

Model: src/rsimodel/{model,delta,cutsets,montecarlo,lco,policies,plots,report}.py; parameters: params/{anchors,assumptions,environments}.yaml; generated reports with per-run provenance tables and machine-readable CSV summaries: outputs/ (headline table: Download original CSV (2 KB)). Stages 1–2 of each allocation use HiGHS through a persistent warm-started model, with scipy.optimize.linprog as the retained reference/fallback path and RSI_SLOW_LP=1 to force it. Stage 3 uses the pinned OSQP solver for the strictly convex normalized tie-breaker, with a numerical fallback. All randomness flows through explicitly seeded numpy.random.Generator instances; every script derives its seeds from stable crc32 strings (never Python’s process-salted hash()), and each anchor’s Monte Carlo draw is keyed by the run seed plus the anchor’s NAME, so results are stable both across processes and under anchor-list growth. All tables regenerate deterministically within a pinned reference environment. outputs/MANIFEST.md records the sha256 of every release artifact, including the canonical Markdown and standalone HTML, plus library versions; it omits a self-referential generating-commit field. tests/test_repro.py cross-checks the committed CSV against the committed report so mutually stale artifacts fail the suite. outputs/report_deep.md and Download original CSV (2 KB) are written by a single execution of one script and cannot diverge. Structural coefficients are ASSUMPTION-class and live only inside named assumption sets.

The integrated model is src/rsimodel/integrated.py, with the analysis module in src/rsimodel/integrated_analysis.py, configured entirely by params/integrated_model.yaml and run by the installed rsi-run-integrated command. outputs/integrated/report.md, 33 CSV tables, and five figures are generated from one in-memory scenario set. outputs/integrated/MANIFEST.md records the sha256 of the configuration, implementation, runner, focused tests, and every generated artifact. Its ensemble uses 200 deterministic named draws per scenario from seed 404. Adding a draw or changing a coefficient changes the manifest; none of that upgrades an assumption to evidence.

Appendix D: Complete model specification

Everything a reader needs to reconstruct the Part I model without opening the implementation. Part II’s cost model is fully specified by its affine form (II.2) plus the anchor table (A.4), with two implementation details: the annualization applies component-specific lives (compute hardware and its replacement launch mass on compute.life_years_space; PV, radiator, storage, structure, and their launch spend on power_systems.infrastructure_life_years, floored at the hardware life — the LCO remains exactly affine in launch $/kg), and each Monte Carlo iteration resolves every anchor once per cached AnchorSet so Earth and space share common physical draws while retaining separate financing anchors. This appendix covers the multisector dynamics and then specifies the paper layer that runs beside it.

D.1 Integrated-bootstrap layer

State space. The implementation has 18 sectors: power, mining, refining, robotics, machine tools, construction, thermal, transport, repair, recycling, interconnects/boards, passives/power, sensors/control, packaging/test, mature logic, advanced logic/memory, process equipment/metrology, and compute. It tracks 17 material categories: O, Si, Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Ti, H, C, N, Cu, Ni, Co, Cr, Li, rare earths, and dopants — 15 elements plus two material classes, so the model is material-category-resolved rather than element-resolved: stoichiometric and process-chemical closure is not checked at the species level. The full coefficient set is the machine-readable specification in params/integrated_model.yaml.

Material and service closure. For material category ee, sector jj, and source/transfer arc aa:

ΔMe=∑sYs,eXs+Ie+∑aFa,ein−∑jBe,jxj−Le−∑aFa,eout, \Delta M_e = \sum_s Y_{s,e}X_s + I_e + \sum_a F^{\mathrm{in}}_{a,e} - \sum_j B_{e,j}x_j - L_e - \sum_a F^{\mathrm{out}}_{a,e},

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

where Be,jB_{e,j} is the amount of material category ee required per unit of sector-jj build, Ys,eY_{s,e} is the recoverable yield from source and process ss, and Fa,eF_{a,e} is material flow across an Earth, lunar surface, orbital, or asteroid transfer arc. Concentration alone does not set YY; mineral form, beneficiation, refining energy, purity, and loss remain outside the occurrence citations. Service closure uses Ai,jA_{i,j}, the sector-ii service output needed to build and replace sector jj. Recoverable lunar and asteroid yields, rather than bulk inventory, enter the constraints. Earth material appears only as the bounded initial strategic-material import stock vev_e.

Process environment and autonomy. For each process jj, task coverage at AI level II is

cj(I)=min⁡{cjmax,cj0+αjmax⁡(I−1,0)}. c_j(I)=\min\{c_j^{\max},\ c_j^0+\alpha_j\max(I-1,0)\}.

(D.2)

Explain equation (D.2)

Task coverage by capability

Unscripted task coverage rises linearly with capability above the baseline until it reaches an embodiment- and process-specific ceiling. The relation is a sensitivity convention for residual intervention, not a measured universal automation curve.

Terms

cj,cj0,cjmax,αjc_j,c_j^0,c_j^{\max},\alpha_j
process task coverage, baseline, ceiling, and AI-level slope. Units/domain: fractions in [0,1][0,1]; slope per capability-index unit.

Indices and local domains

  • j indexes industrial processes.

Operators

  • The inner maximum prevents below-baseline gains; the outer minimum enforces the coverage ceiling.

Validity and assumptions

  • Coverage is smoothly divisible in this approximation and can miss hard threshold tasks.

Relation: conceptual relation. Model layer: process autonomy. Implementation: Implemented in sector productivity and intervention constraints.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

Effective productivity is multiplied by (0.5+0.5cj)(0.5+0.5c_j) — a declared ASSUMPTION-class convention assigning fully scripted, conventionally automated operation half of full productivity at zero unscripted-task coverage, not a measured relation. Residual annual intervention is hj(1−cj)zjh_j(1-c_j)z_j and its sum must fit the scenario budget; the linear form treats missing autonomy as smoothly divisible labor demand and does not represent threshold effects, where one unrecoverable diagnosis, calibration, or repair task stops a line despite high average coverage. Where declared required acceleration gj*g_j^\ast exceeds lunar gravity gL=0.165gg_L=0.165g, the acceleration gap adds centrifuge structural material and parasitic power. The reported centrifuge speed follows

rpmj=602π9.80665max⁡(gj*−gL,0)rj. \mathrm{rpm}_j=\frac{60}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{9.80665\max(g_j^\ast-g_L,0)}{r_j}}.

(D.3)

Explain equation (D.3)

Process centrifuge speed

The required rotation rate supplies only the acceleration gap between a process requirement and lunar gravity, scaled by rotor radius. Processes needing no additional acceleration receive no centrifuge penalty.

Terms

rpmj,gj*,gL,rj\mathrm{rpm}_j,g_j^\ast,g_L,r_j
centrifuge speed, required acceleration, lunar gravity fraction, and rotor radius. Units/domain: rpm; multiples of Earth gg; multiples of Earth gg; m.

Indices and local domains

  • j indexes industrial processes.

Operators

  • The maximum clips a negative acceleration gap to zero; the square root converts acceleration and radius to angular speed.

Validity and assumptions

  • Uniform circular motion and the declared effective rotor radius are used.

Relation: implemented model equation. Model layer: process-environment physics. Implementation: Implemented in process-specific mass and power penalties.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

This is an equipment penalty, not a claim that a whole lunar factory or habitat requires artificial gravity.

Seed sizing. Decision variables are sector capacities zjz_j, annual lunar and asteroid feed pL,pAp_L,p_A, and initial Earth strategic-material stocks vev_e. The linear program minimizes

subject to minimum viable sector capacities, task coverage and intervention limits, service output sufficient for replacement plus one complete second cell, element balances through each scenario horizon, and mining, refining, transport, and energy throughput. Sector commissioning lags and half-ramp loss reduce productive years. Mdigital=5M_{\mathrm{digital}}=5 t represents the software, simulation, industrial-memory, and experimental package; its value is an assumption, not a storage-mass estimate.

The LP can also minimize Earth-import mass or intervention demand, using installed mass as a lexicographic secondary objective. All three objectives return the same central design in every LP-feasible scenario. This is not a Pareto frontier: it shows that the present variables contain no alternative process or redundancy choices capable of trading those objectives.

Dynamic sector-capacity growth. A feasible seed begins as one installed and operating cell — delivery, unloading, site preparation, and first commissioning are outside the model, so seed mass refers to an installed operating nucleus, not a self-deploying delivered package. Each quarter, lunar production, commissioned asteroid production, and recovered retirement enter inventory. New orders use the complete balanced sector-and-material vector of the seed design. For each sector jj, installed capacity KjK_j, operating capacity OjO_j, ordered capacity, its declared commissioning lag, yield ramp, and depreciation δj\delta_j remain stateful. Retired material is recovered by category at the declared 82% fraction. Lunar feed scales with operating mining, refining, and power; asteroid feed additionally requires operating transport. An incomplete packet contributes only the output qjOjq_jO_j of sectors already operating. The reported cell-equivalent aggregate is derived as min⁡jOj/zj\min_j O_j/z_j, and the doubling threshold is first passage of that minimum to 2.0. It is not the discrete commissioning of a second factory’s subsystems and not, by itself, evidence of sustained growth. Balanced packets remain a restriction: the dynamic allocator cannot yet choose an independent sector composition or explicit repair action.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

where ItI_t is the dimensionless capability index at elapsed year tt; I0=1I_0=1 and Imax=3I_{\max}=3 are the declared initial level and fixed-regime frontier; ℓ=0.025\ell=0.025 is capability-index gain per verified-loop equivalent at unit compute signal, unit frontier factor, and unit efficiency; νv(t)=vmin⁡sνs(t)\nu_v(t)=v\min_s\nu_s(t) is verified loops per year after the v=0.85v=0.85 verification yield and the train, data, experiment, evaluate, safety, deploy, and observe stage bottleneck; and ηhw,ηutil,ηalg,ηarch\eta_{\mathrm{hw}},\eta_{\mathrm{util}},\eta_{\mathrm{alg}}, \eta_{\mathrm{arch}} are dimensionless effective-compute ratios. CtC_t is installed compute capacity converted into the model’s compute units, C0C_0 is its initial value, βI=1.25\beta_I=1.25 is the frontier-gap curvature, and Δt=0.25\Delta t=0.25 yr. The train-stage rate alone scales with (Ct/C0)1/2(C_t/C_0)^{1/2}, capped at twice its baseline; the other stages do not automatically accelerate with compute. Every coefficient in this update is ASSUMPTION-class. It is a bounded sensitivity structure, not an empirical law or a forecast of intelligence.

Intelligence above the scenario starting level raises both industrial productivity and autonomy, which raises cell output and future compute. Earth and Earth-fed orbital counterfactuals instead add capacity at constant, scenario-specific build/delivery rates, subtract 0.16/yr depreciation, and impose terrestrial site ceilings. Moon→orbit compute has a 0.5-year lag, a 35% share of new endogenous capacity, and a transport-capacity ceiling.

Debris state. A separate stress test evolves active assets, derelicts, and a fragment index. Failures, controlled disposal, retrieval, collisions, fragment creation, natural clearance, and active removal are explicit. RdebrisR_{\mathrm{debris}} — the five-year fragment creation-to-clearance ratio — is fragments created divided by fragments cleared over the last five years: a flow ratio, not a branching-process reproduction number. Realized clearance is capped by the fragments available, so at an empty fragment stock the ratio reads exactly one. The distributed case multiplies the collision kernel by 0.01; it is therefore a declared topology test, not a derived property of heliocentric space.

Orbital lifecycle and common-cause controls. A separate capacity-equivalent mass-flow sensitivity implements Equation (24) with the nine reported states operating, degraded, awaiting service, under repair, cannibalized, salvaged, recycled feedstock, disposed waste, and uncontrolled debris. Repairs return capacity only after service start, completion, and repair yield; salvaged mass returns to production only after recycling yield and manufacturing capacity. Collision losses and disposed or recycling waste enter the irreversible-loss diagnostic, while successful debris retrieval subtracts from it. Tests require nonnegative stocks and conservation after external deployment is included. This layer does not model mission-specific capture trajectories, qualification of repaired hardware, or species-level recycling.

The common-cause control sensitivity evaluates Equation (27) against explicit node capacities and hazard sets. Its shell-state controller maps crossed thresholds to deterministic actions: pause deployment and dispatch removal for creation/clearance, hazardous-descendant, or derelict-mass violations; increase spacing and reserve maneuver propellant for conjunction or maneuver violations; reduce cluster caps and isolate failure domains when tracking or communications degrades; and tighten disposal reliability or retire a shell after disposal violations. Zero-valued conjunction, maneuver, tracking, and communications metrics in the current table mean “not simulated by this run,” not observed safety.

Scenarios and uncertainty. The four named cases are terrestrial rehearsal, lunar strategic-material bridge, strict lunar-only, and Moon–asteroid network. Their horizons, AI levels, import caps, intervention budgets, and source commissioning dates are all explicit in the YAML. Each 200-run ensemble uses stable crc32 names from seed 404 to draw independent log-uniform multipliers for service productivity, bills of material, lunar and asteroid yield, depreciation, lag, and autonomy gap. Frequencies across those draws are design-space occupancy, not empirical probabilities. Tests verify dimensions, nonnegative balances, strict-lunar infeasibility, finite-import-stock behavior, gravity overhead, aggregate-capacity doubling, named-draw stability, and the debris threshold. outputs/integrated/MANIFEST.md binds the configuration, implementation, runner, tests, tables, figures, and report.

Analysis module. src/rsimodel/integrated_analysis.py adds derived diagnostics over the same declared coefficients, inventing none: terminal-window endpoints (retention at horizon, final-five-year net capacity change, import-pool exhaustion timing); strategic-import-stock resolution; zero/freeze intelligence-coupling ablations; the installed-mass-versus-aggregate-doubling oversize frontier (simulate_capacity_growth(initial_cells=f) installs f cell-equivalents of the fixed minimum-mass design); per-draw ensemble diagnostics over the identical named crc32 draws (failure reasons, binding-constraint frequencies, Spearman sensitivity); and an elastic-relaxation infeasibility certificate that interrogates the exact seed LP through a shared matrix builder. The expanded module also compares independent allocation and explicit repair, observable knowledge/autonomy outages, process-environment profiles, finite-mass shell debris, policy and structural-shock sweeps, shelf-limited electronics architectures, symmetric dynamic economics, and composition-changing robust-seed Pareto designs. The full table set and five figures regenerate with the run, including the full sector trajectory and an 80-year central extension. These diagnostics add structure and falsification plumbing; their coefficients remain assumptions pending empirical calibration.

D.2 Ten-sector model

Sectors and units. n = 10 sectors, ordered: power, mining, refining, robotics, machine_tools, electronics, thermal, transport, repair, recycling. Capacity K_j is in abstract capacity units (K_j(0) = 1 for all j unless stated); sector j produces q_j output units per capacity unit per year (q below is the central set after environment q-scaling for the lunar architecture is applied via environments.yaml; the tabulated q is the pre-scaling set value). Repair and recycling are service sectors: their rows in A are zero, and their outputs are consumed as described below.

Time. Discrete steps of Δt = 0.25 yr (0.5 yr for cut-set enumeration), default horizon 35–40 yr. This layer has no construction lags, commissioning delays, yield ramps, or minimum efficient scales — all its outputs are stylized model outputs, not engineering timescale forecasts.

Imports. m_i(t) = B₀ · e^(−t/τ) · φ_i, with per-sector cutoffs (m_i := 0 for i in the cut set after the cutoff year). Stockable sectors’ imports flow into the stockpile; non-stockable flow into the current balance. Mars: stockable imports arrive as synodic batches of size m·(2.14 yr) every 2.14 yr.

Allocation (per step): three-stage lexicographic optimization. Variables: builds x ∈ ℝⁿ₊, wear-repair u ∈ ℝⁿ₊, recycling activity w ∈ ℝ₊, stockpile drawdown d ∈ ℝⁿ₊ (d_i = 0 for non-stockable i), growth floor g ∈ ℝ.

Stage 1 — maximize g subject to:

xj+uj−δjKj≥gKj∀j,uj≤δwear,jKj∀j,∑jAijxj+sf∑jAijuj+𝟏i=repair1ηrep∑juj+𝟏i=recyclingw+oiw−ρiw−di≤qiKi+mdirect,i∀i,w+ηscrap∑jfwear,juj≤ηscrap∑j,cfc,jδc,jKj,di≤SiΔt. \begin{aligned} x_j + u_j - \delta_j K_j &\ge gK_j && \forall j, \\ u_j &\le \delta_{\mathrm{wear},j}K_j && \forall j, \\ \sum_j A_{ij}x_j + s_f\sum_j A_{ij}u_j &\\[-0.2em] \quad + \mathbf{1}_{i=\mathrm{repair}}\frac{1}{\eta_{\mathrm{rep}}}\sum_j u_j + \mathbf{1}_{i=\mathrm{recycling}}w &\\[-0.2em] \quad + o_iw-\rho_iw-d_i &\le q_iK_i+m_{\mathrm{direct},i} && \forall i, \\ w+\eta_{\mathrm{scrap}}\sum_j f_{\mathrm{wear},j}u_j &\le \eta_{\mathrm{scrap}} \sum_{j,c}f_{c,j}\delta_{c,j}K_j, \\ d_i &\le \frac{S_i}{\Delta t}. \end{aligned}

Stage 2 holds g at its optimum and minimizes dimensionless stock draw ∑iωidi\sum_i\omega_i d_i, where ωi\omega_i is the inverse of a same-unit scale based on current supply and available stock, normalized by the largest weight. Stock is a buffer, not fuel, and the objective is invariant to changes in sector row units.

Stage 3 holds the stage-1 and stage-2 optima within solver tolerance and minimizes a strictly convex normalized action norm:

Operators

Validity and assumptions

  • Flows are held constant within each explicit time step and use consistent annual units.

Relation: implemented model equation. Model layer: dynamic state transition. Implementation: Implemented after each lexicographic allocation step.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

with shelf life L_i (electronics 5 yr central), capacity cap C_i = c_years · Σ_j A[i,j] δ_j K_j (replacement demand), initial stock S_i(0) = s_years · replacement demand at t = 0, stockable sectors only (robotics, machine tools, electronics, repair). Common-cause shocks are applied after this deterministic capacity update; the stock cap is then recomputed from the damaged capacity. Reported timestamps and shock-log timestamps are the step end t+Δtt+\Delta t. The headline realized growth is

Realized balanced growth

Realized system growth is the worst sector’s post-shock fractional change over the step. It is reported separately from the allocator’s pre-shock target so disruptions cannot disappear from the headline rate.

Indices and local domains

  • j indexes productive sectors.

Operators

  • The minimum selects the slowest sector after shocks.

Validity and assumptions

  • Pre-step capacities are positive and post-shock and pre-step states use the same capacity units.

Relation: implemented model equation. Model layer: dynamic outcome reporting. Implementation: Implemented as the reported balanced-growth diagnostic.

Canonical definitions and scoped units.

while the allocator’s pre-shock g*g^* is retained separately as g_alloc.

Depreciation. δ_j = δ_wear,j + δ_catastrophic,j + δ_obsolescence,j + δ_logistics,j per environment (environments.yaml), anchored entries resolved at geometric mids (deterministic) or loguniform draws (MC), one shared draw per anchor per run. Obsolescence is included on the reading that K is frontier-equivalent capacity (A.1’s five-quantity separation).

Shocks. Per step and per shock class: N ~ Poisson(rate · Δt) events; each multiplies K over its sector group by (1 − f), f ~ U(f_lo, f_hi). Rates jittered ±30% per MC run (ASSUMPTION).

Outcome definitions. Expanding at year 30: realized post-shock g > 0 at the step ending at year 30 — the instantaneous, weakest endpoint; it does not preclude import- or stock-supported growth or near-zero absolute capacity (a minimum-viable-scale criterion needs an authorial threshold and is queued). The pre-shock allocation endpoint uses g_alloc and is diagnostic only. Sustained: realized g > 0 at every recorded step ending in years 25–30. Earth-import cutoff: a separate central-set ensemble with all Earth imports cut at year 30; the endpoint is realized g > 0 throughout 30–35 (stock draw permitted). LEO retains capture feed and is labeled accordingly, not as autonomy. Balanced doubling (headline replication metric): first t with λ(t) = min_j K_j(t)/K_j(0) ≥ 2 — unit-invariant, requires every sector to double in its own capacity units; it is not a claim that a complete second physical seed has been commissioned. Aggregate doubling (continuity diagnostic): first t with Σ_j K_j(t) ≥ 2 Σ_j K_j(0), measured against the supplied K(0) — unit-dependent, reported alongside but never as “system replication”. Both doubling metrics are reported over all runs that ever reach the criterion and conditioned on year-30 survivors — the difference is the doubled-then-failed class.

Binding sector and co-binding. At each allocation step, each material-balance supply is relaxed by 1% and stage 1 is re-solved. The finite response Δgi\Delta g_i is unit-invariant because both the perturbation and row quantity scale together. Every positive response within 5% of the largest forms the co-binding set and shares fractional credit. If all responses are numerically zero, relative slack supplies a display fallback only. The baseline and allocation-policy comparison use the same definition.

Central-set structural coefficients (ASSUMPTION-class; conservative = central with A×1.35, δ×1.4, τ=10 yr, and reduced repair/recycling/stock scales; optimistic = A×0.75, δ×0.8, τ=25 yr, increased scales; full machine-readable sets in params/assumptions.yaml):

D.3 Consolidated notation

This register supplements the local “where” paragraphs; it does not replace them. A symbol’s definition is scoped to the model layer shown in the last column. Reuse in a different layer requires an explicit subscript or a fresh local definition. Roman labels inside subscripts identify named categories, bold capitals and lowercase letters denote vectors or matrices where stated, and i,j,e,s,a,h,k,m,n,pi,j,e,s,a,h,k,m,n,p are local indices whose domains are defined beside the equation that uses them.
